reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and unique place. The sea changes color continuously and creates spectacular effects. To visit absolutely.  A place to respect for its uniqueness

reviewsWithKeywords.title: *Not for nothing one of the most beautiful beaches in Greece!"
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The drive down to the beach offers fantastic views. The color of the sea incredible; beautiful but hard to walk pebble beach and no bars, umbrellas or sunbeds. Toilets available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, stunning beach⛱️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a step ride down the hillside you will come to the beautiful, white pebble beach. You can park your car at the back of the beach free of charge. Absolutely stunning crystal clear blue water. Lots of fish swim right near the shallow part of the beach. Great for snorkeling. Make sure you have beach footwear to use in the water as the stones can be painful to walk on. A stunning location. Would highly recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning, we didn’t drive down to it as hire car would never have made it up winding hills again! It can also have some dangerous currents from what we heard.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picture perfect view but no beach experience.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful view. Postal perfect picture but nothing more. Don’t expect to be able to get in the water if you have kids. Extremely strong waves and dangerous for anyone who is not experienced. White pebbles. Bring water shoes otherwise it will be difficult to walk around. No facilities available. No shade or umbrellas. Bring your own.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unbelievable!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: FantasticWe had gone by boat Unbelievable beauty and relaxation of the mindImposing and parallel beautiful colors of the water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A little disappointed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sea, with all shades of blue, but....the beach has no assistance, no umbrellas, or anything. Just a small, strictly closed wooden building. A MASSIVE landslide overwhelms it and pushes its debris almost halfway to the beach. I was told that a small bar only opens in July and August and that the problem is the landslide. We "folded" on Petani beach, equally beautiful and of which I attach the photo.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views from above are incredible and well worth a look, the beach is lovely but it is much more comfortable on Antisamos in my opinion.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning beach and a must when visiting Kefalonia. Crystal blue milky sea with lots of pebbles so take water shoes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, with spectacular viewsAlthough a tad cold when we were there, clear sea. Enjoyable few hours. Could do with a little café/beach bar although did look like there is one maybe bit too early in season. Drive down fabulous views, we even passed a heard of goats on route

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bring all your own stuff
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myris beach is stunning, from above. That's why they take all those amazing photos from there.The beach's is still just a (very stoney) beach. We went as part of a 3 sight excursion  and we were able to drive all the way down the very twisty road to the beach itself.  We arrived just after lunchtime and already there were a lot of cars parked. Our (Greek) driver and guide was very annoyed that, despite it being late May, no beach facilities were open and he felt he had let us down. No bar or cafe open, no toilets open save one single gents toilet, no loungers or parasols. No doubt these will be available later on in the year but until then you will need to bring your own food water, and some shade with you. Beach is very pebbley and gritty so walking can be difficult, beach shoes are a must and under the water underfoot is still treacherous. Water clear, ideal for snorking but nothing to see as nothing grows amongst the grit and pebbles. Without the bar or loungers a couple of hours at the most. Really not worth the effort  but you do get a lovely photo on your way out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Myrtle!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach in Greece! We can't wait to visit it again in July 2024! Kefalonia forever!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mediterranean essence
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Impressive viewpoint of this beautiful beach, possibly the best known in Kefalonia. Small parking lot for about 8 vehicles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in the world, in season it is best to arrive quite early 9/9.30am, umbrellas and deckchairs at reasonable prices, possibility of bringing your own umbrella, don't forget your beach shoes. Beautiful water, kiosk that doesn't do hot dishes but above all packaged sandwiches

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Superiority
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in Greece. unique crystal clear waters beautiful scenery that will amaze you on the left side of the beach go see the cave

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impossibility of vehicle access to the beach in the summer
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful beach but in the summer access and parking is almost impossible. It is the only beach in which the only thing we managed to do was to go dead-end with the car, without stopping anywhere, and to return to the main road, having escaped for a little dead-end and scratches on the vehicle. No control over the way cars park in the space, creating dead end traps. I'm sorry we didn't swim but I won't go again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach...Unforgettable experience...!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with turquoise waters, which are crystal clear, white pebbles and white sand. Be careful in deep water, especially for those with small children. Driving down the road and seeing her from above literally leaves you... with your mouth open. I have visited it many times in the past and I always leave excited, even on our last visit (June 2020) when due to the corona pandemic the beach bar was not working, there were no sunbeds and umbrellas and the people were quite limited. The cave to the left of the beach is impressive. It is a beach that anyone visiting Kefalonia must visit. You have to go...don't miss it...well worth it!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Heavenly....an absolute must see. Rent a car and go to a piece of paradise. Afterwards, stop for lunch in the nearby restaurant. Alexandros. Impeccable. Local lady who speaks perfect Italian. Very kind

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, watch the currents
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach, which is relaxing. The sea was fairly choppy and no one was in it, which I was told is usual for Mytros Beach. I managed to have a quick swim, but came straight back in due to the strong undercurrent and I am a strong swimmer, so please be weary of it. There is a cafe, toilets and a lifeguard on duty at the beach. You are no longer allowed to go into the cave at the fair end of the beach, due to falling rocks. There are view points of the beach up at the top of the cliff, at both sides, which provide a fantastic view of the beach. 100% recommend, such a beautiful beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful during the day, spectacular at sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pebble beach similar to Antisamos, but with very few fish visible. A small cave can be reached with a few swimming strokes (land entrance closed due to risk of landslides). Very hot even in June-July because it faces west, on the other hand it offers beautiful sunsets. Very crowded from late morning, it is best to get there early to park near the beach, otherwise you will have to stop along the access road or in the paid car park. In the inns on the beach you can eat well at average prices.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Suggestive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water has enchanting colors and for 10 euros a day you get 2 sunbeds and an umbrella. Bar very poor for food, better to organize from home. Mainly made of white pebbles, for me who love sand, it is definitely not my favorite beach but it should be seen at least once.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoyable Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful.  The water is crystal clear and when we were there, the water was warm.  You must have water shoes because the beach is very rocky.  Also, they do have beach chairs but not many.  Also there is a little cafe you can get something to eat and drink, and they have bathrooms and shower.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You are the most beautiful in the world!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you think of a beach, the most beautiful one you can imagine....yes, it is the most beautiful in the world!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blue clear water, small cave and a private like feel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful pebble beach with clear blue water and a small cave for exploring. Cafe and snack bar on site plus umbrellas and seats for a slight fee.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely looking beach but be careful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On our way to Fiskardo we stopped off and had a look down to Myrtos beah. From distance it looks like white sands, but the locals informed us that it's actually small pebbles.It does look uber-gorgeous, but another warning we were given is that there can be some nasty undercurrents off the beach, so please be careful when swimming especially the little ones.Also, it's a mini rally stage to get down from the main road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A corner of sky in the sea 😀❣️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking colours, crystal clear water, a very long beach with few umbrellas, therefore very free 👍, but equipped!The only really sad flaw: management of the refreshment point is chaotic, poorly stocked and of poor quality, very impatient managers!!!!!It's probably not the place for them, because in a sunny paradise only smiles and kindness can reign.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but not the most beautiful on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The directions are not very clear and we struggled to get there. I recommend arriving in the morning before 10am because the car park doesn't have many spaces. The beach is very large and spacious, with pebbles which require shoes. Unfortunately the day I went the sea was rough and not being a fan of waves, I only got my feet wet. The sea water is clear with a beautiful blue color, and immediately becomes deep. It is equipped, there are showers and a small bar where you can buy drinks and sandwiches. Definitely a beautiful beach but, in my opinion, not the most beautiful on the island, as it is considered

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful island. Beautiful beaches. Good food and nice people.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were in Skala.Beaches are partly sand and there are stones where the sea begins. The water is very clear. We rented a car for 3 days and explored the island. Also took a boat trip to Fiskardo. The capital is very beautiful to see once. Myrthos beach is also great.😍. Would love to come back again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible. It is important to know that it is necessary to bring booties or diving shoes, there is no sand. The sea has a fascinating temperature and color, I recommend going mid-morning to appreciate the beauty with the full sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must-to-do with caution (E-Bike)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rode down to the beach on our e-bikes and what a wonderful and colorful memory it was. The beach is long and therefore not crowded. There is water from the showerhead for showering. The road is more good than bad. Caution is advised but it is still a must-do.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Approaching Myrtos beach, you can see what all the fuss is about, simply breathtaking and stunning.Beach is glorious, rock foreshore which requires the special beach shoes for optimal experience, however waters are crystal clear and great for swimming.Snorkelling available is different areas , including near the cave.Beach chairs available for rent, parking okay , but get in early to be sure, toilets and shower, and cafe also available. Overall, fabulous experience and probable number 1 must visit in Kefalonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach Kefalonia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water is clear and Beautiful to swim in and look at.  Please note that it is a pebble beach so would recommend some wet shoes as it can be difficult to walk on.When you look down from the main road viewing point it looks like sand. Parking is plentyful but can get very busy in the afternoon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Busy busy busy. Lovely beach with one little cafe bar. Sunbeds €10 for 2 with umbrella which considering its a famous beach, is really good. We had a lovely peaceful day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing and memorable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach I have been to and I have been to several around Greece. The water is quite cold though but nothing to deter you from being there. The waves are strong and the water can be deep as you enter. I wouldn't recommend it for small children unless supervised at ALL times. There are toilets there and a canteen to buy some water and snacks. The umbrella and 2 beds costs 10 euro with an extra 3 euro for each additional bed. The main thing to highlight is the drive, which is not for those scared of heights. Small cars are recommended, as the roads are narrow, dangerous and in some cases fit one car. So if you come across another car, it will be challenging to reverse or move to the edge due to cliffs with minimal barriers. You may see mountain goats on your drive which add to the areas beauty.  I would recommend going but only if you're ok with all the above.  We loved it! Just beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: STUNNING SCENERY BUT NO FACILITIES
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Views speak for themselves.  Beach is stunning and the water is crystal clear. However, nowhere to park car except on beach which I think is truly awful.  No beach bar or toilets.  So if you go there, make sure you have food & drink with you and a can to pee into!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: In the blue... painted blue💙
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We toured almost all the Greek islands but Myrtos seen from above on a sunny day is inexplicable!!Pure wonder

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The bathroom here overcomes the inconvenience of access
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water with incredible colors, but in August be aware that this beach (a single beach) is super crowded. We arrived on 2 wheels and luckily! The road to get to the car park is bumpy, downhill, unprotected and even frequented by coaches!! So if you don't want to ruin your day, set the alarm and arrive early. I imagine that in the low season it is a dream because a bath here is absolutely worth it. Not recommended for children who don't know how to swim, because I took three steps and I mean 3, and I already couldn't touch it anymore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Azure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views and the color of the water is simply stunning. The beach is a pebble  beach and when its windy the waves are too rough to swim in. There is a lifeguard on duty and serviced sunbeds and loungers but your are free to setup on your own also. Would recommend coming well supplied as the road up and down is steep.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Stunner!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach on the Island of Kefalonia, Greece. Beautiful drive and the hike here has to be one of my 3 best in the Mediterranean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: STUPENDOUS !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing view !! Beach with beautiful colors! Worth a visit but you have to get down early at least before 10am otherwise the umbrellas are sold out! Worth seeing! The best beach in Kefalonia!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like a poster
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely amazing beauty. Like a movie, like a travel show. But I caught it on a windy day and I couldn't enjoy the water as much as I would love to. You can also have parachute there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: PARADISE, GO EARLY AND BRING FOOD FROM HOME
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A paradise as long as you go there by 9.30 in August, bring food from home and choose the day carefully due to wind and rough seas especially with children.A surreal place of breathtaking beauty, at sea it feels like being in space... indescribable and absolutely worth seeing!To be seen in the morning at 9.30 in August because at 12 it loses its poetryThe tavern here only has horrible pre-packaged cold sandwiches, expensive and terrible

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, but chaotic and overcrowded.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach and the water are beautiful, the colors are mesmerizing, so much is true. What they don't tell or show you is the surrounding chaos. The beach is crowded with coaches full of groups coming down. There are sunbeds and parasols everywhere, but around 11:00 none of them will be available anymore. There are people arguing over parking spaces. Guides from the buses are screaming at people in cars to secure their spot.The road leading to the beach is very steep and everyone and his mother is trying to get down there. Also the people that shouldn't drive on these roads, leading to dangerous situations.So 5 stars for the beauty of the place. 1 star for the experience.If you don't mind big crowds, you're going to have a great time. If you don't like crowds of tourists, your experience could be a little stressful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Truly the most beautiful beach in Kefalonia together with Petani Beach!Very large beach, both equipped and free, spectacular blue water.Unmissable!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely necessary to visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is large, it has sunbeds and umbrellas ( 2 sundbeds and 1 umbrella 10 euro) but  you can also bring your own umbrella.  The  beach is covered with small and large pebbles, you should bring special footwear. The water becomes suddenly deep  with big waves. The blue shades of the water are  fantastic!You should come at the first hours of the morning because becomes crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: To be seen. But…
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is definitely a five-star beach, without any ifs or buts. Before arriving at the beach it is recommended to pass through the Myrtos Beach view, which allows you a panorama of the blue sea full of Myrtos. The beach has one big flaw: the sea. And I'm not referring to the color, but to the fact that finding the sea calm and flat is a lottery. I believe, but have not verified, that the best time is around 8:00/8:30 in the morning at the latest. Finding parking is not easy, you have to go down and hope that someone is leaving while you arrive. Beach made halfway between pebbles and sand. Worth seeing though if you pass through Kefalonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach - well worth a visit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with aquamarine blue sea. Best to arrive early to get a sun-bed and good parking spot. Sea was lovely to swim in but waves powerful and slopes away steeply. Not very suitable for small kids. Would definitely recommend visiting but arrive early!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Caribbean Blue in Kefalonia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The road to the beach is in good condition, practicable by any car, and the scenery wonderful. The car park is full after 10 o'clock. There is a beach bar, and the sunbed fee is 10 Euro, but there is enough space and privacy for your own umbrellas. The water is an unreal blue, the scenery dramatic, and a lot of powerful big waves. The entrance to the sea is steep, and the currents quite strong.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rubbish everywhere. Disgusting abuse of somewhere so beautiful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Over crowded , over used litter everywhere. I was so disappointed and angry. How can anyone let such a beautiful beautiful setting get so trashed.   The cigarette butts , plastic and other rubbish in the sea was gross, it made me feel sick.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White pebble beach and spectacular sea, not transparent due to the seabed which goes down almost immediately, but beautiful colour. The only flaw is that the road is a bit bumpy, otherwise a very pleasant day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach, scarce facilities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Named in top 10 world beaches by many magazines and agencies, Myrtos certainly deserves it.Dramatic setting between two huge cliffs with gel like aqua marine water is best seen from the road view point up. Zig zag paved road (10 y ago it was gravel road) takes you down there, so no problem to access it. Once down, parking is the biggest problem - we circled almost half an hour to get a spot (parking is free).Beach is long and wide, so despite huge number of people in July peak season it didn't seem crowded. Water is movie like, simply gorgeous.However, there's only one establishment selling food and drinks and renting sunbeds. Lines are huge and food junk with inflated prices (ordinary bakery stuff, didn't see nothing below 5 euros a piece). We stayed some 2,5-3 hours and moved to Antisamos beach which has much more facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach, crystal clear waters. If you visit Kefalonia this beach is a must. A hidden paradise residing in Greece.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Colors of paradise, hellish journey
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Undeniably crazy colours, but everything else is a nightmare: the merciless crowd at the car park after 10.30am, sunbeds and umbrellas sold out already at dawn, a small bar to serve an entire beach, cars everywhere along the road which make the dangerous journey, and we traveled by car, I can't imagine with a scooter. Pebble beach and immediately high water, rock shoes recommended. Defining the beach as "equipped" is an understatement.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magnificent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice and long beach, with beautiful colors. It has some umbrellas but most people set up their own. It is definitely worth a visit for anyone who hasn't been, certainly the times to arrive before 11 are the most suitable for parking and to sit wherever you want!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enchanting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The glance between the turquoise and blue of the sea makes you forget the color of the sky.Before you even arrive you want to dive in.The road to get there, even if it is asphalted, is not easy due to the cars and the presence of sand. Especially if you find yourself visiting it with a scooter. Convenient to leave it anywhere to admire this wonder up close..The beach is characterized by smooth white pebbles. . Better to wear appropriate footwear.The sea is gorgeous. Found a windy but pleasant day and slightly rough sea. But the spectacle of colors and the view that opens up to you cannot be compared to the difficulties encountered.The undertow created on the pebbles emits a sound never heard anywhere in the world. It seems that the sea has its own voice... what can I say, simply wonderful, to the point of returning again before leaving

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Viewed from above. Quite busy in high season and parking difficult. There are even coaches going down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Colors never seen before
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Suddenly paradise. From above, before arriving, you are left breathless: you don't see turquoise like this anywhere else. Once on the beach you are surrounded by the beauty of the colors. Impressive

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful white pebble beach. For my taste, it's not very wild, that is, well organized with umbrellas and services and very busy.Definitely worth seeing but out of season

reviewsWithKeywords.title: To admire rather than swim in
reviewsWithKeywords.text: More beautiful from above than up close. Strong chromatic contrasts between the light blue of the sea and the white pebbles, but also dangerous due to the step that forms a few meters after the shore and the undertow that is present in case of slightly rough seas. Not suitable for snorkeling. Acceptable establishment prices, limited parking, the road to get there is asphalted but not exactly simple.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach in kefalonia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazing beach, well worth the hair raising drive down! Parking is a bit tricky but it’s so stunning, it’s not to be missed. A beach bar and sun beds and showers are available. A fantastic day out!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A sea of relaxation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White sandy beach with pebbles. Accessible barefoot. Turquoise sea.Pros: umbrella with two deckchairs €10, large free parking. (I recommend arriving early)Flaws: small bar for the large and renamed beach where it is located.The sea immediately becomes deep. To be considered for families.Ps: there are no waspsOverall great experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful from above, azure blue, pebbles, simple meals, no guardrails on the way there
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Positive:- very nice view from above to the bay, beautiful- azure blue water- pebbles but reasonable to walk on- showers on the beach- free parkingNegative:- the road there has hairpin bends and no guardrails, which is why we have only been here once, we thought it was dangerous, especially with oncoming traffic- Seawater deep quite quickly- Not a restaurant for an extensive lunch, but an opportunity where you can get some simple things such as hot dogs, ham/cheese sandwich, pizza slice, etc.come early because of parking- We prefer Petani, a similar bay but with good restaurants and a better road with guardrails. The view from the top of Myrtos is the most beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A panorama that leaves you speechless
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach with breathtaking views, the water is a surreal blue (as seen in the photos) and you can immediately notice the contrast with the blue of the sea offshore. The beach is sand mixed with pebbles (I recommend shoes) and there are free showers and cabins. The road is steep in the final stretch and the terrain leading to the (free) parking is gravel. There is only one well-stocked bar and two sunbeds and an umbrella cost €10.It would be advisable to check the winds before going there, as we found the sea to be too rough with high waves, so much so that it was difficult to swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Viewpoint
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach looks amazing and breath taking from the view point. But it's a long winding road to get down to it. And then when you get there you find out that it's lots of white rocks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not naturally beautiful water color
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great place for everyone, except that young children should drip in the sea under the care of adults due to the high waves...beautiful color of the water, clean beach..there may be a problem with parking the car

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has an amazing view. I recommend to all to visit at least one time. The single inconvenience is that there are so many rocks there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beach not to miss.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is definitely a beach worth adding to your itinerary. I would recommend going early if you are driving as parking is limited. I arrived at 10.30 and there was plenty of spaces. The drive down is long, with air pin bends but don’t let this put you off. The road is in good condition and as I’ve noticed most locals are patient with holiday drivers. When you get down there the beach is your reward. Shingles beach, the best thing I packed was beach shoes. There are clean toilets, parking is free. There is a bar serving cold/ hot food, reasonably priced. Probably one of the best beaches I visited, if not the best.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So much could be improved
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was lucky to visit Myrtos on a non windy day and really enjoyed the water. However there is much to improve upon:The beach bar is operated by the municipality themselves instead of auctioning to a private entity as the majority of other beaches do. So the people that work there are civil servants and they have such a mentality too. At 17:30 they all go home leaving hundreds of people who thought they cameto an organised beach, without food and water. Furthermore, the sunbeds are not even close to enough for the number of visitors the beach gets and are placed very far from the sea, close to the beach bar. As a result, visitors who cant find a free sunbed / umbrella, bring their own and sunbed customers cant see the waters. Finally, the beach bar had run out of most items by 15:00, seems nobody cares to order stock according to the demand due to the monopoly of the situation. If you dont like it after all, you can walk up a kilometer which is where you parked, drive your car to the nearby village and get something to eat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but not the first
reviewsWithKeywords.text: According to most it is the most beautiful beach in Kefalonia and one of the best in Greece. In fact the water has beautiful colors typical of the Mediterranean sea but in my opinion it comes after Petani beach. There is a choice between a free or equipped beach, the prices are modest, in line with those of Kefalonia, between 10 and 15 euros for an umbrella and 2 sunbeds. Like many beaches on the island it’s made of pebbles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views, great beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach with stunning views! Sea was nice and warm too. We went at 5pm and although it was still very hot, it wasn’t too busy. The roads are tight to get up and down there so if you are not a confident driver be warned! Some great views on the drive otherwise. There are changing and WC facilities down there which are free to use which is handy too. Definitely worth a visit if you are in kefalonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t believe the hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Horrible beach, parking awful, just dump your car anywhere down the cliff road, sticking out? No issue just put on hazards. The toilets are Dirty, one ‘eating drinking place’ whucdikd hot dogs or pastry things, and juice etc. little seating and what there was was filled with cool guys with feet up, if you want an instra photo fill your boots, but there are better beaches with better parking, I fail to see why this is voted best beach, do NOT believe the hype, stay away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely day at this beautifully located beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Anyone visiting Myrtos Beach in July and expecting it not to be busy has some seriously unrealistic expectations I would suggest. Yes, the beach was busy but to be honest I've seen more packed beaches in the UK at the first sign of sun. I can also see that if you drive down it is perhaps quite stressful given the hairpin bends and amount of cars but this is not the beach's fault. We took a taxi from Fiskardo, which cost 45 Euros each way and took approx 40 minutes. The beach is in a beautiful location. It is a shingle beach, so beach shoes were useful. The sea was blue, clean and clear. There were plenty of sunbeds, which were very reasonable at 10 Euros for 2 plus a parasol. The beach cafe was clean, well stocked with drinks and snacks and we didn't experience (or see) any long queues. Toilets are of the portaloo type but again were clean and stocked with toilet paper. Perhaps previous reviewers had a particularly bad experience but it was certainly not ours, we had a lovely day. The earlier you arrive, the quieter it is.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach.  We went early, arrived at about 10am and parking was fine.  Got ourselves a couple of beds and a shade and stayed there all day.  The sea is warm (July).  There is a beach bar at the back of the beach and also toilets and showers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nightmare with stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nightmare parking Impossible Parking Crowded Badly organised Nightmare Never go there Plus sideGreat views Stunning location Just to crowded with buses and cars parked everywhere!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like nothing you have ever seen!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is paradise!!! The most beautiful beach I have ever been to! The moment you walk down steps you find yourself in heaven. There are no words to describe this beauty!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short visit but definarely worth it as a point of interest if you are driving.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning beach, pure white pebbles creating a spectacular array of colours of the sea. Well worth the visit just to see it. When we went swimming was not possible due to the waves but it was still very busy. Be prepared for limited parking even though the parking area along the beach is big, and very narrow and windy road down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better beaches on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is no doubt this is a beautiful beach.. however the decent up and down is treacherous .. cars parked everywhere, extremely tight hairpin bends, dealing with large coaches, no barriers, people walking up and down.. When we finally managed to get down, we drove on straight back up.. there are thousands of people here with only one cafe bar and a couple of portable toilets.. so I can only imagine how dirty the sea water must of been. Not a pleasant experience at all and there are more beaches that are just as pretty if not more so with far fewer people and better facilities. Save yourself the trip, it really is not worth it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with nice amenities. Sunbeams, snackbar, restrooms.  The view from above the beach is spectacular. The water was incredible!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great photo point from the top but that’s it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A little disappointed. Stunning views of the beach from the top but when you go down you realise it isn’t a sandy beach but white pebbles which give it the white sand effect. Very uncomfy to lie on as there are no sun beds here. The many coaches bringing tourists descend on the beach so like ants and the entrance into the water is impossible without water shoes and then the water is cloudy with poor visibility for snorkelling.  It makes a great photo but that’s it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beach like many on kefalonia it has crystal clear waters and is very picturesque, ideal for families, rock shoes are advisable like most beaches its,a mixture of sand and small stones I would definitely recommend going

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtakingly beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtakingly beautiful!The weather let us down on the day we visited , nevertheless the beach was so beautiful and so peaceful.The beach is very clean and there is a small cafe for drinks .After watching the movie Captain Corellis mandolin, which was filmed on this island, it was amazing to actually visit and view such gorgeous locations.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Possibly my favourite
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely hit the spot for me … just beautiful!Obviously your experience will differ depending on the weather and number of other visitors, in our case the variables were just right.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach is Wonderful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wind? Waves? Mega-Crowds? Danger? Not for us. We completely enjoyed this stunning, amazing beach experience. Water shoes are a must, along with water and snacks. I would go back in a heartbeat!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise in motion
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Early morning start for the entripds.. we jumped in to the rental car and fired up the engine, it spurted in to life as ever reliable. Our plan today was to navigate the mountain passes to Sami.. As we drove we experienced an invasion of our senses, the smells of kefalonia forever in our senses and thoughts. The lush countryside playing out in front of our eyes, the locals sitting by roadside cafes drinking coffee and slowing their heartbeats even lower in the flat line island. As we passed we could smell the thick coffee beans and the hum of distant tractors in the fields Sarah turned to me and asked what time it was.. I didn't know and further more didn't care, time stands till here. We only think about time when the sun is up and it's food time. So I turned left towards Porus. Continue over the mountain passes and eventually we spy Myrtos beach. What a wonderful sight and at the same time a frightening one.. Our little fiat Panda now turns in to a 4x4 mens machine as we traverse the hairpin bends and wild mountain goats springing to attention around the vertical drops. After navigating what appears to be something out of the Italian job bends we see the beautiful Myrtos beach and guess what it's free parking and the beach is clean and welcoming. It has small pebbles but you can place your towel down and immerse yourself in to these pebbles. In high season they put out sun beds and there's a lovely beach hut selling wares and food/drink. There's also clean spacious toilets and changing rooms not like the grubby UK resorts with filthy toilets and amenities. We settled down and relax.. sun, sea and lovely company in this paradise of Myrtos beach. When we were there they were paragliding which was a sight to see. Bad points. Nil. Unless you call the hairpin experience. Everything is great good old kefalonia keeps on giving.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great looking beach. Little hard to park in high season. Go with sea shoes or with a boat.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great extra large with white pebbles beach. Really beautiful colour of the water. Scenery is amazing. Not great to walk on the pebbles though. Also a bit hard to park in high season.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolute bliss.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited at the end of May and were blown away. This has to be one of the most beautiful beaches in the world!The beach was easy to access by car. There were a couple of small pull overs on the way down to admire the view and there was plenty of free parking at the bottom (it was only the start of the season so I'm not sure how busy it would get in the peak summer months).The beach is pebbly and not sandy - I would recommend wearing some sea shoes/sandles as the drop into the water from the beach is steep and quite difficult and uncomfortable to walk down/up with bare feet.There were no cafes on the beach but plenty of small shops from which you can buy drinks etc.from at the crossroads as you turn down to the beach from the main road.Advice - bring swimshoes, bring plenty of drinks/snacks and an umbrella as there is no shady areas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: More than worth the drive.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful white stone beach. Sea was cool but really refreshing. There’s a free car park at the bottom.  Not sure if there’s a bar in high season. There’s a small building but this was closed up. Word of warning - it gets hot down there and unless you take your own parasol there’s no shade to be found. The sun bounces up off the white stone as well.  It’s hot, and we were there in May!  It’s not warmed up yet! It’s a totally relaxing beach though. There’s no music blaring, no one shouting. Just the beautiful view of the mountains and the sea. When you leave stop at the top to take a look at the stunning view. If you don’t like heights hold someone’s hand!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Intsa worthy and spectacular!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The descent wasn’t as bad as expected after reading other reviews - decent road surface compared to some other beach tracks we’ve explored whilst in Kefalonia but if you’re a nervous driver you might find it a bit daunting. Appreciate that we visited early in the season so didn’t have any problems with meeting vehicles coming the other way or parked on the road. The view points on the way down provide breathtaking vistas of the beach and Instagram worthy photo opportunities! Striking white beach with spectacular turquoise waters. What’s not to love?!The beach itself is made up of millions of small beautiful white pebbles and not sand, so be prepared and being suitable shoes for wearing into and out of the sea, otherwise you’ll be crawling out on all fours in an ungainly fashion and looking like you’re on the way home after a heaving night in Malia (not my husbands best look 🤣)The caves to the left of the beach are pretty cool. Plenty of parking (although this may get very busy as the summer progresses). Facilities weren’t open, but we expected that given that it was early in the season. The beach was lovely and clean - other reviews indicate that’s not the case and again, perhaps so as the beach gets busier but all in all, it was well worth the journey from the south of the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular views but take appropriate footwear…
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went in may when the beach wasn’t busy and nor was the road in…I imagine it could be different in the peak season. Steep descent down…but the road better than many others we have done this week. Lots of (free) parking. Stunning views. Crystal clear water and a great cave off at the far end (south). Toilets weren’t open though yet (just a dodgy portaloo) and although it looks like there will be a bar, not open yet. Can imagine it would be an amazing spot to watch sun go down. Main recommendation is to take good beach footwear…the stories about the pebbles are true. Have to confess I was crawling out of the sea on all fours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picturesque
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic view from above is a must before venturing down to the beach, the beach like most on the island is a mixture of pebbles and sand, the water is crystal clear with a blue tint offering a picture perfect image.Would recommend to anyone visiting the island

reviewsWithKeywords.title: "Top 10 In The World"??????
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped on the road well above the beach for a photo op. Yes, the location surrounded on three sides by steep sandstone cliffs is quite spectacular and the azure waters of the Ionian Sea amazingly beautiful but I don't believe it ranks in the world's Top 10 beaches as our guide intimated!!!! Great photos though!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach on the planet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We landed here after hearing how wonderful the beach was. Although we are out of season and nothing was open here, the beach was deserted so we had it to ourselves. It didn’t disappoint- we went in a fairly windy day and the waves were amazing. And the blue of the sea - the pictures don’t do it justice. I can imagine in summer it would be packed but late April and September, the locals say is best time to come. Things are more open and weather is not windy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Totally deserted. Had beach pretty much all to ourselves. Plenty of parking. Not sandy, but small rocks. Once in water was delightful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unbelievably  stunning beach. A must visit. We visited out of season and it was virtually an empty beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Indeed a spectacular beach accessed by a steep twisting road Very well organised with beach beds, showers and toilets. Has a small cafeteria which is ok for a light snack and drinkPebbles and not sand but despite that well worth a visitEnjoy the views from above

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not as amazing as it’s reputation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went because of the hype, it was quite a trek to get there by car down treacherous cliff edge mountainous roads. The colour of the water is certainly stunning. To be fair, once we got there we found out the water us choppier in the afternoons. For us, the water was so tough with huge waves crashing before hitting the beach we didn’t actually go in. Took some photos and left. There is one bar/snack facility down there, don’t know prices. Also several camper vans parked up where people were staying on the beach. One to tick off,but just wouldn’t bother to come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must do in my opinion.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We last visited here 16 years ago and it's really good to see that the facilities down here have improved vastly,good clean toilets nowadays and a decent restaurant.As we only wanted a cooling swim on the drive back to Lassi from Fiskardo we didn't bother paying for sunbeds,but unfortunately none of us had brought the definitely required sea shoes to get into the water,so quite a painful difficult experience to get to the water.The sea was relatively calm during our visit so a delight to enjoy the cool clear waters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning myrtos beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow what can you say absolutely stunning beach, beautiful trip down to the beach stunning views , the sea is the most amazing blue colours never seen so many different shades of blue

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is one of the most stunning beaches I've ever seen. The views from the top of the cliffs are amazing. There are plenty of amenities on the beach, food, drink, changing rooms, toilets and showers. There was also a lifeguard. Definitely worth a visit, especially when the waves are up. The beach itself is pebbly so I would recommend beach shoes or flip flops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful white pebble beach at the bottom of a winding hill road. Plenty of sun beds, good clean toilets and snack bar. The sea is crystal clear. A little difficult to get in and out as you sink into the pebbles but once you’re in it’s refreshing. A must visit in Kefolonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow, amazing beach and fabulous facilities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazing Greek beach with crystal clear water. Excellent toilet facilities, free parking, changing cubicles and a large cafe serving food and snacks. Highly recommended!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dirty Sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would say if you came here today you’d have to avoid the scum and what looks like effluent when you get in the water. Great shame, maybe boats dumping their load, not sure but not pleasant either. 😢💩

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning turquoise beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach with a really nice turquoise water surrounded by a huge white coast. We enjoyed it so much that we went there twice during our stay.For the first day, the water was calm so we could swim around, but in the second day, the fun was unleashed by the big and nervous waves that were smashing the beach!!! Also, on Myrotos beach, we had the most incredible sunset.Unfortunately, in August, it is very crowded, full of cars parked along the road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful bit of heaven!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove from the resort of Lixouri to Myrtos beach, what a scary drive around the very winding mountains , lots of gear changes, but well worth it to see a little piece of heaven! You have to arrive before 10am if you don’t want to have to park on the road and walk down the cliff side.  There are toilets, sun beds  and umbrellas (10 euros for 2) as well as a beach bar which sells cold drinks, ice cream and other snacks. Bring swim shoes as it is a very pebbly beach as with many in Kefalonia if you truly want to enjoy the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Truely stunning beach BUT not family friendly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach, views and everything but if the wind is inward blowing, you CAN NOT swim as the waves are 2 to 2.5 meters high. It's not family friendly at all as the water depth goes from knee hight to 2+ meters deep in a space of 2 meters! There's a great little cafe. A must visit but just be careful with the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice for photograph taking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An overrated mess!  The beach is wonderful for the photograph taking, and there is an access road to it, which works unless there is a bus in the way, when it becomes suicidal.  Beautiful blue water, whereas the beach itself  is a dusty overheated pot with pebbles.  Just like everything else, parking is improvised.  Recommended for rented vehicles only.   At the end of the beach there is a small cave and it is interesting to swim through it, although there is a sign saying hat access is forbidden due to rock slide, which no one pays attention to.  The entrance to the sea is the best close to the cave.  Nice to see, take a photo and never come back.  Kefalonia has a serious issue with roads.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: dissapointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place takes a great picture due to the stunning colour of the water and the contrast with the white beach. However, beauty is only skin deep and in every other respect this is not a good beach in my opinion.The beach is composed of chalk pebbles which are quite painful on the feet and the water is often very choppy and the water gets deep quickly, so beware, particularly if you go with kids. The water looks so cool because it's full of chalk dust, but this makes it impossible to see anything in the water unless you swim pretty far out.Lots of tour boats come here and hang around off the beach...and flush their toilets into the water! I swam out and had an unfortunate encounter with a load of poo!You can hire loungers, but if they are all taken then you might be able to hire parasols from the lifeguard hut, otherwise you'll spend your whole time under the relentless sun. There is a beach bar but didn't go in there.The whole place is in a pretty stark and unforgiving setting and it's like you are on a beach in the middle of a desert. Didn't enjoy the experience at all and there are far better beaches elsewhere on the island.Parking is also a pain.If you are passing by, then pop in for a while if you can park, but no point in making a special journey. I won't be going again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best sunset in the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water is beau, you can find place in the afternoon on chair and umbrella… the sunset is amazing, Bring your drinks and speaker and enjoy a perfect sunset

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Exceeded expectations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach. From other reviews I wasn’t expecting to enjoy myself so much, but apart from the pebbles being bothersome (make sure to wear shoes to walk down to the water), the beach was quiet and clean and the water absolutely stunning in both colour and temperature. I arrived at 1130 and had no troubles getting a park (free to park). I did not find the swell at the beach dangerous when I was there. The view from the lookout, or even if you pullover driving up to the top, is incredible. Highly recommend this beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but difficult
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is gorgeous, pebbly and it’s pretty painful to get into the water without a good pair of water shoes. I have knee problems, so wouldn’t recommend it for others with the same dilemma.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach and beautifully clear water to snorkel in
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We hired a car and drove there from Skala after visiting mellisani cave. Stunning views as you drive down to it. Looks deceptively like white sand but it’s actually pebbles. Cars park all along the road that winds down to the beach. I would recommend that you drive right to the bottom then start from there to find a space as there are people coming and going all the time.  I would highly recommend buying a parasol from the shop in the little town at the top before you drive down  (around €13) as there is no shade unless you hire a sunbed.We just wanted to snorkel and had beach shoes with us so when we reached the rocks it was easy to clamber around. Spent a wonderful couple of hours snorkelling around the rocks in the beautifully scenic bay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take a photo and move on!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The colour of the water is dramatic no doubt. But as others have said, take a photo and move on. Horrible road down to the beach with no barrier. The beach itself is all stones and the sea gets deep really quickly. Water was very rough (though no wind) and I certainly wouldn’t recommend going in unless you were a very strong swimmer. Definitely not good for children, at least when we went. There are life guards on duty though which tells you something. Car parking ok and there is a beach bar. There are much nicer beaches elsewhere on the Island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a Wonderful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a wonderful beach. One of the best I have ever seen or been to, anywhere. The view from the high road was amazing and hardly changed as I came down to sea level. On this day there were about 150 cars and possible 400 people. Beachside bars, shops, water rinse station and bathrooms. Everybody was having fun and getting a "little cooked" in the 40 degree temperature.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Do take a photo from the above, then move on!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach, no doubt, but not suitable for swimming (too rough, not clear water)  or relaxing by the beach (too pebbly, too busy) during high season.  I am sure it is lovely if you visit there like May or September? A car park was full by 1030am in mid-July and frankly speaking, there are many other wonderful beaches in Kefalonia.  Although there was NO WIND on the day we visited, the sea was still so rough that we could not swim for long.  Plus the water is murky and has no visibility.  Be very careful if you have little ones - it gets so deep so quickly -like 1 meter in from the beach, you cannot reach the bottom.  I would recommend you take a photo from the top of the hill, take in the gorgeous view, and then swiftly head to Assos or other places on the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bring water shoes! So glad we did but the beach is almost all small river rock and is very challenging to navigate bare-footed and in the water. There seem to be new facilities at the beach with a bar/cafe, restrooms and changing rooms. The water is ridiculously warm but not as clear as some of the other waters in greece.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A magnificent beach that needs beach shoes to cope with the pebbles. Busy though and the beach bar has little to offer.Come early to get parking by the beach, otherwise it could be a steep walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in the world.  However, due to it being open to the sea, with no island protection, it has extremely strong undercurrents and is difficult to swim.  Great to visit, and relax, not for swimming.  Pretty decent beach bar too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spoilt by sewage
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have been to Kephalonia many many times and Myrtos was my favourite beach. Very sadly we went in June and there was raw sewage floating in the water. We can only assume that a boat or boats had emptied their bilge tanks into the water and it was disgusting. There was s**t in the sea and lots of it. We got out very quickly and showered and left immediately.The beach itself is stunning - yes it looks like white sand from the top but it is white pebbles when you get down onto it. You need beach shoes to get into the water. Sadly this wasn't our only experience of the water being dirty, last year we were there and there were bits of food floating around. I don't know how they can police this but they cannot let the boats empty their tanks into the bay. It really was disgusting and very dangerous if you were in there and swallowed the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Uncomfortable but “wow” view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful view but that was all. Uncomfortable sunbeds, no tavernas or bars. We went back to Gradakia beach after 1h.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Looks great and inviting from the road
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have driven passed Myrtos beach a few times in the past and the beach looks so inviting so much so that during our last stay in May we decided to drive down the winding road to the beach. When we parked we were very surprised and disappointed that the beach was made up of large pebbles and no sand.There weren’t any facilities such as bar's, cafe's consequently we stayed for 5 minutes then drove away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful!! White pebbly beach and turquoise waters, can be very busy and parking difficult so would go early. A must see while there. Great restaurant in the village just before the turning for the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and breathtaking coloursPeacefull and amazing place to visit!When in kefalonia id a must!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's alright
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Need to arrive by 10am to rent a sunbed and brolly, / or bring your own - no shade anywhere. We got really lucky at midday, the rental girl took pity on us with 3yr old. Fairly steep shelf into the sea, strong waves and very strong pull back out - not the best place for small kids but we had fun for an hour. High point was the wow factor when the beach swings into view from the road. Great to visit if you're near or passing, but the hour drive up from Skala broadly wasn't worth the effort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views from above, overrated beach below.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely worth stopping at the viewing point along the road on the way to/back from Fiskardo and Asos (would recommend visiting both) to look out at the coast line and beautifully blue sea, but not worth going specifically for the beach and swimming. The sea has a VERY strong backwash and you can get easily knocked over. It also gets deep quite quickly, so the waves break on you, which really put us off swimming. I would suggest the beach it’s more suited for a strong and confident swimmer. Also worth noting it’s a pebble beach. It wasn’t too busy when we visited around 6pm and there was plenty of parking. The drive down is steep and winding, take it slow if you visit. Overall, we definitely preferred the beach from the viewing point along the road, than spending time on the beach below. There are nicer beaches across Kefalonia to sunbathe and swim at. We would recommend Antisamos (near Sami) and Skala or Kaminia (in the south).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a cool beach, busy and the sea can be lively. Nice beach bar and showers, parasols, toilets etc. gets very very hot and not a great deal of natural shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blue blue sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the bluest water beaches I’ve been too and we’ve been to Caribbean Maldives USA. This is definitely a beautiful place. Strong waves make it hard for weaker swimmers to get in but it’s soo pretty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Overrated beach with very hairy drive down/up. Stop and view from top and carry on to a much nicer beach just down the coast  Agia Kyriaki (must quieter and calmer) The beach gets very busy so best to arrive before 10 am. Rough sea when we went - do not go in with sunglasses!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach in the world!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach I have ever been to in my life! Incredible green and blue waters that impress you from the first moment! very deep sea but if you are lucky and there is no wave it will be one of the most beautiful experiences of your life!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: way-way overated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Way-way overrated! The water may look like this from a drone, but when you swim, it's not as clear at all. It gets deep very close to the shore and there are only stones, not sand. There is only one bar operating on the beach, so everything is expensive and you have very little choice for food and beverages. The umbrella and long chairs are rented for 10 EUR, but they keep renting them multiple times per day (when we left, at noon, another couple came and they rented the same umbrella again, which I am not sure is legal). Anyway, it;s nicer to see the beach from one of the belvedere spots along the road, than to spend time on the beach. Totally not appropriate f or children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, lots of space but no nicer than others in Kef
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We finally made it onto the beach (rather than just looking down on it!)  last week & we had a mostly pleasant afternoon. As others have said, the beach definitely looks better from the road above. It’s nice enough when you drive down to it (yes the roads are a bit hairy but then that’s Kefalonia) but no prettier than other beaches I’ve visited. A vast bay means there’s plenty of room for everyone. My husband was stung by a jellyfish as soon as we entered the water which was a bit of a downer but he survived! So we stuck to the beach after that. A nice beach to visit just to say you’ve done it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach for sure.Come early if you want to have a car place and sunbeds, or take your own umbrella with you. It’s burning hot without, no shades.Beach is a mix of sand and pebbels

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach Pebbles but smooth completely round ones white The day we went down to myrtos sadly so had the jellyfish so couldn’t go in The lifeguard was telling people to stay out of the sea shame as it was lovely and calm it’s usually quiet rough

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Family of 9. Very rough water the day we were there.  Very rocky beach that was difficult to walk on.  Water shoes recommended. Fee for use of umbrellas and chairs. Refreshing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful beach authentic and brilliant scenery although is majorly busy therefore water is not very clear and is costly and difficult to get a sun bed but all in all a amazing beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sunset. Beautifull beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sunset. Beautifull beach. It has both sun beds and no sun beds areas. The water is light blue and the beach is full of small white pebbles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lovely way to cool down after a lunch in Assos/Αsos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing rock beach, now with life guards, kiosk, showers & free parking right beside the beach. Take your rock hopping beach shoes!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: ABSOLUTELY STUNNING
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking from high above, even more stunning down by the water, super refreshing in the sea. Unforgettable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely amazingly beautiful beach with picture postcard views. It is not a sandy beach it is very smooth pebbles, we took beach shoes to make it easier to get in and out of the water. The pebbles were also surprisingly comfortable to lie on, just arrange the pebbles to suit your body shape. A must place to visit if your in Kefalonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, long drive down to it!! Plenty of parking available. Small beach bar, not sure of prices / stock as we didn’t use it. Changing rooms and toilets available next to it.The beach is long and wide but you need to take your beach/rock shoes unless you’ve got thick leathery skin on the soles of your feet!! 😂No sun beds or parasols available when we visited, so if you can bring along your own!!The view down to the beach from the roadside above is stunning, well worth the drive out alone. 😎👍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow. This truly is a stunning beach. Probably one of the most photographed beaches in the world, and you can see why. White glistening sand and turquoise blue waters. This really is a taste of paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picture postcard beautiful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning. Vast. Painted turquoise sea. A beach not to miss.Plenty of free parking..Easy to find. We stopped here for a couple of hours enroute to Fiscardo for lunch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Did not disappoint!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely unreal, beautiful and worth the trip- I have to recommend you take a parasol, beach shoes and food water as there were no facilities but it was worth the drive over

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super visit on your Way to Asos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Defently s super visit. Nice cave and super water With deep blue Ocean With Nice small gravel rocks that gives Nice Sound on the wawes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Look around!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visit other beaches on Kefalonia before saying 'this is the most amazing beach on the island/in the world'  because, honestly, its not. The colour of the water IS amazing but so is it at Petani/Atheras and multiple other beaches. Atheros has 2 taverns but no beds, with a swallow beach, not tidal but that's the appeal. Petani has 2 taverns, beds, kayaks, pedalos, deeper water but no strong currents, and is way prettier a beach than Myrtos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach!! Narrow road and no restaurant there 🥳
reviewsWithKeywords.text: People say it is the most beautiful beach of the island! I saw it from above and it looks amazing. I will drive down these days. I was told to swim in the middle and be cautious of the drag of the waves. Best to be safe than sorry and not swim at least at this beach 🥳🙏🏼 Cristal clear waters!! There are no bathrooms, chairs or restaurant. Bring your water and food 🙏🏼🥳

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but hard to walk on with peddles, also strong current so knocked off feet quickly not suitable for children or non swimmers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful View.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On our Holland America tour of Kefalonia, we did a brief photo stop of Myrtos Beach.  However, we did not actually drive down to the beach.The views were beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just insanely beautiful!! A MUST!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever seen. The color of the water, the overlook, everything about it is just incredible!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I am not sure why but I was bit disappointed. To get there it is a hard-core as the road  is narrow and not for the people with fear of hight!! From above it is a picturesque place but on actual beach the sand amd the water  is not as spectacular . There are better beaches in Kefalonia but still Myrtos is a must see. Beach bar is very basic with drinks,hot dogs and crisps.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice views but there are better beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice place and relatively quiet but not suitable for young children as the incoming tidal wash is quite strong and it gets very deep very quickly (less than 5-10m from the shore you are no longer standing). The water is very murky so snorkeling isn't good. Overall a nice place but probably not worth the effort to get there unless you're nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A most fabulous beach for the family which has strong currents so may not be ideal for toddlers and small children. A blue flag with lifeguards and lovely cafe, with plenty of free parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Only from above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As I write on the title....This beach worth only from above! Just take couple of photos from above and go.I have visited so many beaches around the world and still can not understand why this beach is so famous and has also so many awards.First of all is very far from everywhere, at least 40 minutes driving in a not so good road. Secondly the road that leads you to the beach from the main road is in very bad condition and narrow and dangerous.Thirdly when you arrive you realise that the beach is full of big white pebbles which means that you can not place your towel anywhere.The time I went it was not organised but still nothing special even organised.The beach as well as the water were so dirty, full of plastic bags and bottles and many other thingsWater was foggy and cold and as many say dangerous. With no wind there were large dangerous waves.One time for photo is enough.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing but difficult!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most visually spectacular beaches you will ever see. Amenities-wise though, one of the most lacking beaches in the world!Do take some swimming/diving shoes because the stones really hurt the feet! Also, take some umbrellas, refreshments for the day and anything else you may need to sustain a beach trip because there are no shops on the beach. And parking is a bit of a mission too when its busy.The sea is quite rough, and there are some currents that won't be suitable for small children to swim in, but worth the visit for the sheer beauty of the place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, terrifying drive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Firstly, the drive to the beach was terrifying: Winding roads with large drops, sudden bends and no barriers. As someone who is afraid of heights, this really tested me and  I was surprised to see the road so poorly maintained when it the beach is obviously so popular. (Perhaps I am an outlier given that this isn’t mentioned more prominently in other reviews, but if you are not a comfortable driver and/or afraid of heights be warned).The beach is busy so get there early to get a sun-bed and decent parking.Not a lot of amenities on the actual beach - just one beach bar with some basic snacks and some toilets (which were well maintained).Swimming was the highlight with beautiful water against the backdrop of the cliffs - I truly found it special. Water does get deep quickly but when I visited, waves and currents weren’t an issue so seems to depend. Probably not very suitable for children given it gets deep quickly and takes a bit of an effort to get out with the step incline of pebbles.All in all, loved the beach but the sketchy road to the beach needs to be improved and I don’t think I could have my nerves repeat the experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picturesque yet pebbly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most stunning beach I’ve seen in Kefalonia. But it’s not suitable for kids as the waves is too high and current is too strong. The beach is pebbly and it’s recommended to bring aqua shoes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beyond expectations
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beauty of this beach and its surroundings exceeds any expectation, but unfortunately there's a lot of people (and I mean A LOT) who also know about this place... My suggestion? Go early in the morning, around 9 am; you'll be able not only to park you car by the beach, but also to enjoy until midday or so, a really stunning place. If you're not traveling with a cooler, a basic canteen for coffee and refreshments will keep you hydrated while you're at this one-of-a-kind-place. Don't miss it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better than the pictures
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went here August 12/21.  Beautiful to look at. They day I went the waters were rough. Nice white rocks at the shore.  This area was hit by a flood as a result the facilities are extremely limited.  There are some chairs but not enough for the amount of people attending this high tourist attraction.   The parking is a nightmare. I recommend water shoes as this is a rocky beach. Must see

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Outstandingly beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hold onto your hat as you experience the winding and at times pretty terrifying track down to beach. But when you get there it is worth the effort. Parking can be a bit tricky at busy times but once you are on the beach and in the sea it all feels worth it. The colour of the sea is magnificent and even though the waves can be a bit rough at the shore but the water is warm and if you swim out a bit it gets calmer.There are sun loungers and umbrellas for hire which are necessary if you don’t have your own as there is no shade on the beach and the sun is unrelenting. There is also a beach bar and showers. But really the sea is the star of the show.If you have small children who can’t swim then just be aware that the water gets deep quite quickly and the force of the waves can knock you over at the water’s edge.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worth the hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach has a beautiful landscape when viewed from above. Once down there, the actual experience deteriorated, as the sun loungers are not enough, and laying on the pebbles is rather uncomfortable. Swimming is fun in the waves, but getting off the sea is rather perilous, especially as waves can be massive and the stony ground not ideal to offer you good support.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go out of season or be prepared for crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful turquoise water and lovely setting. Go early or out of season. Bit too busy for us. Parking a challenge, no sun beds left and no eating facilities so take water and a picnic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing landscape, beautiful beach, clean water. There are some sunbeds and umbrellas, but most people bring their own. There is no shade, so be prepared.There was no beach bar when we went (there was one behind the umbrellas under construction), so bring water etc. We arrived around 11am and it was already quite busy. There is some parking space just before the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but dirty water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Whilst stunningly beautiful, both from the approach road down the cliff and the beach itself, this wouldn’t be my favourite beach on the island. Amenities are under construction and for a crowded beach, there was relatively little atmosphere (no bars etc). Most disappointing of all was the cleanliness of the water - too many boats at anchor offshore have left a wide trail of sewerage that lingers in the waves making swimming an unpleasant experience on this visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Marvellous.  Deserves all the hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Firstly, get there early (would suggest by 9.30) to ensure you get a place in the beachside car park (not obstructive) rather than having to park in the steep road leading down.  Despite its popularity it's relatively undeveloped: paid for sunloungers and umbrellas are relatively few and their style bel ends in well- they are set back from the sea.  Most people are sitting on the beach itself.  More areas of  sand on the beach than we expected, mixed in with small  white pebbles so easier on the feet than most N Kefalonia beaches.  No cafe or beach bar although one seemed to be in early stages of construction.  Sea is warm and clear, although be warned it slopes away dramatically.   Overall, An essential stop on any Kefalonia trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kefalonia 2021
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach at Greece. The water was so clean and the place was peaceful . The only problem is that there is not a store to buy something to eat or drink

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Parking problem, no atmoshere whatsoever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is made only for viewing from a distance. Its amazing. The drive downstairs is very bad, with a lot of holes in the road and a lot of curves ( asphalted). Downtairs you will two parking sides ( only stones not asphalted).There is not enough parking for the people visiting. So al lot of people parking it on the road which you have to drive to get downstairs. Not a happy thing to do along the abyss.We where there 10:30 (EEST = greece time) and after 10 minute  searching we where able to get hold on a parking place.  Do not come here after 11:00 (EEST) you are to late and will not find a parking downstairs. This is only in the months of july and augustus.  Otherwise you will need to park near the abyss. The beach bar is being build at the moment ( 2 augustus 2021) so bring your food with you. There is a car driving up and down to get some food if you make and order, but it is very busy. The guy where you can make an order stand near the showers. I did not see any toilet.The beach it self is very dirte which a lot of stones, bring your swimming shoes with you. The drive to myrtos was very fine but the beach there was no atmosphere whatsoever downstairs.  Left after 2 hours. You have to visite myrtos because thats where kafelonia is known for.Good luck!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful to look at, hard to swim in
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From the viewpoint, the beach looked so beautiful that you thought it was a dream. However, it's really hard to swim in because the bottom is full of big rocks/pebbles, and the strong waves kept crashing you against the rocks. It gets deep quickly. The water is very "cloudy", so you can't see the sea bottom or even your hand/feet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Truly stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most amazing turquoise sea with large waves. Though it is an uncomfortable pebble beach and no swimming. Quite a steep drive down but worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped off at the viewpoint above to marvel at this amazing beach. The colours are so impressive, it almost doesn’t look real. A must-see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunning. The colour of the sea is unbelievable have never seen such a turquoise blue sea!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Large family beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: À large very family oriented beach, rather nice but not exceptional. You can try to escape to the west extremity to find a naturist compatible area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OVERRATED!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very disappointed with this beach. The sand looks like a construction site, there is no infrastructure whatsoever (bar, sun beds) and hills around it are not that nice. Go to Antisamos, much better!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEST FROM ABOVE
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I give it  a 4 because, although stunningly, breathtakingly beautiful from above, when you get to the beach it is all white pebbles.  Whilst they in themselves are so, so lovely, they are hard to walk on.The beach into the sea shelves quite quickly and is not such a good place for young children ... nor for anyone who isn’t a fairly good swimmer.
