There are a lot of underwater currents there too ... so whilst it’s a lovely beach, it can be a challenge, particular when the surf is up!  I’ve been there when the sea has been as flat as a pond and have floated quite happily in the aqua sea ... I’ve also been there where the sea has tried to claim my bikini bottoms as I’ve tried to get out!   In fact, if you have mobility issues, Myrtos is a bit of a no, no.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Cephalonia quite a long time ago (when it was and hopefully still is) unspoiled & HAD to visit this beach for snorkelling and a swim.From a distance, the beach & see look stunning, but it is not sand, it is small pebbles and the water is such a light blue colour because the cliff walls are (I assume) chalk, so once you get into the water & try to have a look underwater, you can't actually see anything hahahahaWe were also warned about a jellyfish invasion, so imagine my horror when snorkelling and my right arm waved through what felt exactly like the top end of a jellyfish - my friends all fell about laughing when all they heard through the snorkel was "WHAT THE **** IS THAT?!?!!" only to discover that it was a discarded plastic bag which as the exact texture of a jellyfish! Hey hoGreat place - Cephalonia was (and is) a wonderful place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don’t miss out on this fabulous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We called here as part of a day tour.  This beach is as beautiful as the pictures of it are. Well worth a visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Road closed cannot visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not sure why no one else has written these to save people time but the road is closed, we tried to walk down and another point the road is fully closed and says not safe to walk down - not sure if the road has come away or there has been landslides like in Assos ( also don’t bother visiting as roads closed due to damage from landslides also)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning. Must see it from above to appreciate the blue sea. Beautiful drive around the coastline. Watch out for the random goats

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best viewed from above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An absolutely beautiful beach viewed from above. I was on my way to Fiskardo so I didn't really have the time to actually go down to the beach. I was told that it can be very busy and that the view from high on the cliffs was the best feature. Certainly, I'd recommend it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great views from above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is obviously the most famous. The views from the mountain are stunning and the drive up and down as fairly straght forward. I would recommend proper swimming footwear as the pebbles can be quite painful. Nice place to visit but head to Makris Galios if you like sandy beaches. The water is more wavey than Makris Galios.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. The sea has all different shades of blue which is amazing, really cool to swim in (but be careful of the rough waves!), never seen a beach like it before. Not loads of choice for food but that’s okay for me, prices weren’t too bad either. We got a taxi to take us there, it was the more expensive option but meant we got to avoid the steep drive down and had no hassle with traffic getting there or back. Really recommend as a must see in Kefalonia!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Raw beauty and force
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is stunningly beautiful, even more so when the waves are huge. If you use your common sense and watch them from the shore you'll be witness to a great display of the beauty and force of nature. The whole experience is beautiful: the many shades of blue in the water, the thunder of the crashing waves, the small droplets of water the wind brings on your face and the smell of the salty sea.Adding to what two previous reviewers said about the guy that "tried to win the Darwin Award", he was eventually rescued by a helicopter after staying 6 hours on a small anchored raft with a lifeguard, riding 3-4 meter waves. May sound fun but I'm sure it's not.Take caution when swimming here, even when the waves seem small-medium, as the water is deep and there is a current pulling you back into the water when trying to get out, so you'll have to fight it a little. As a bonus, exiting the water you'll step on rocks that will prevent you from exiting elegantly. More common would be exiting doing the Australopithecus walk or sometimes even on all fours.If you accept those things and are aware of and respect the power of the sea here, you'll have a great experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach with huge waves!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such beautiful blue sea. It was a bit rough when we were there and you couldn’t swim in the water but the waves made great photos!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunningly beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is well worth a visit but be aware it’s not for swimming. It has dangerous currents that pull you out. There was a lifeguard but he was constantly asking people to come out of the water.There is only a small beach cafe selling drinks and snacks, no restaurants and the toilets were pretty grim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Respect the force of nature
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Reading a review left two days ago when some idiot went against the lifeguard’s warnings into the sea as it was getting dark, I feel compelled to leave a counter review that properly rates the beach and sea and experience versus the people trying to win Darwin Awards.  The waves are powerful, and you should only enter the ocean after waiting for the larger waves to pass (I believe they come in patterns of 7 at a time?).   I wouldn’t let small children swim there as the waves do break violently , and mediocre swimmers need not apply.  But the beach and ocean there is perhaps the most beautiful I’ve ever experienced, and if you respect nature, you will be rewarded by an awe inspiring vast turquoise expanse.   There will always be families who do not recognize the strength of the ocean and these waves in particular... but it should be immediately obvious by first observing (if only people all took the time to do so...).   I would NOT let small children frolic by the shoreline, just as I would not encourage toddlers to pet crocodiles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrthos beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our time spent at myrthos beach was excellent: the waves were spectacular and the sunset was magnificent.This is a place where we will definetly come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Be very careful when swimming we saw a horrific incident
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Today is the last day of our holiday and we wanted to see the sunset at Myrtos Beach.  The waves were spectacular as was the sunset.   However there was one man swimming in the water alone.   At first it appeared that he was having fun but as the light faded it was clear that he was unable to return to the beach.  A crowd developed and various people tried to assist including locals with life buoys, flash lights, long lines etc. We are not aware of the fair of this young man but it was a horrific scene.   We did not know what to do so felt the best we can do is to warn others here. Please take extreme care if considering to swim here, especially is no life guard is on duty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach on Kefalonia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was with my girlfriend for 2 weeks in Kefalonia. And I can say it was the most beautiful beach, that I seen on the island. I have visited other beaches, but this one was  amazing.RegardsAndrew

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful blue
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunning and the bluest sea ever. It is not however good for swimming or even just a dip to cool down. The waves and current when we went were very strong and knocked my husband and teenage son over straight off after about 1.5 meters in. They loved it though and it became a challenge to get past the breaking waves! My daughter found it scary and after one try wouldn’t go back. There is a lifeguard. It is definitely worth visiting for the view but I couldn’t spend all day there as couldn’t really enter the water safely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beach so spectacularly blue you have to pinch yourself hour after hour to check you are not dreaming. The water is immensely clear and the blueness goes on forever. It is a cove surrounded by luscious green mountains - with mountain goats for added Greek authenticity and the white sand is like silk upon the soles ofYour feet. The waves are strong and the current powerful which makes it difficult to get out for a swim but it is immensely fun playing around in the waves on the vast shoreline. There are umbrellas and sun beds for a small fee of 3.50 each and a little beach bar with showers and toilets. I would recommend getting here before midday as the car park got quite busy. On the way down to the beach you must stop off at the viewpoint and film the panoramic views of the mountains meeting the ocean - I have never seen a view like it.  OnlyA couple of warnings would be there are paragliders which land on the beach so be careful to stay out of there way and be careful with children playing in the sea without an adult. As I said the waves are powerful and will. Drag you under if you are not careful. I cannot recommend a beach to go to more highly than this for a perfect peaceful and fulfilling day on your travels.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best thing about this beach is viewing it from the top which offers a truly spectacular view.The road down to the beach is bendy and busy as is the parking.We arrived at 11.30 and beds were plentiful but within an hour none were available.The composition of the beach is made up from coarse sand and becomes pebbles nearer the Sea.The waves can be high and the drop is quite sudden.In a normal season without the travel restrictions I’d imagine a very busy beach.There was One refreshments vendor which was always busy.The sun beds (2) and shades were reasonable at €7 for the day and we’re sanitised before use.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach - steep drive!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The white stones create an azure sea which in August was perfectly cool and refreshing. Get some sane shoes because the stones can hurt one's feet a bit and an umbrella is a must, and at times rentable with longer. The scenery and the drive memorable.  Make sure to capture a groupie from the view up, waaay up above!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, would go later in the afternoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sea- such a vivid blue! The sea was wavy but we managed to stay in line with our bags. We arrived around 4:30 and the beach was still busy, especially the car park, but we managed to get a parking spot close to the beach whereas other cars parked half way up the hill. The beach was still busy when we arrived but we managed to get an umbrella and 2 sun loungers which was fab as the sun was still strong. I would recommend going early or going a bit later when people might be leaving so you can get an umbrella as it is hot! There are more beautiful swimming spots around but this is still worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking view Cold waters and waves . Make sure that you will visit that beach early so you will find parking easily . The sun beds are some how for safety reasons (because of the waves) a little bit away from the waters. It is strongly recommended to wear special shoes for the small rocks that will make your beach walk a little bit annoying. I noticed that there are lot of yellowjackets around the subbed area so please be careful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Views are amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The drive down is interesting but the views are stunning. The parking is grab a space where you can. I can see why it is photographed so much as the views are stunning. A word of caution the sea was rough when we were there and it gets deep very quickly so watch out if you have toddlers. There is a small cafe on the beach which is very reasonable priced - worth a visit for the views

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice peisage from up but not so good no interesting  7€ sunbeds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice peisage from up but not so good no interesting i first of all is a rock beac and if you don’t have slippers you break your feet, the parking is very bad is free but you don’t have any place , you can use sunbeds 2 and 1 umbrella 7€ or free withyour owns,, the water from thw white rocks i think calcar or ... is white but not clear like antisamos beach or other , the best peisage is fromUp

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing view 'from a distance'.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unbelivably many tones of blue and great for view and photos but not much fun swimming in. Pebble stone entry and big churning waves makes entry and especially exit tricky almost dangerous. I had to grab my little kids and pull them.out of the waves and later on watched many adults struggling and tumbling in the waves. Amazing photo background but not bery practical to swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good beach. The view from above is magnificent giving onto a clear blue sea. The beach in itself is nice too. Very rocky so I recommend a sturdy pair of shoes. The water is quite warm and a beautiful translucent turquoise blue. Not too many people either which is great. No restaurants or toilets around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picturesque
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a really beautiful beach and saying anything else would be a lie. However, if you intend to go there, don't forget your aqua/swimming shoes as we did! The rocks are pretty, but not comfortable to walk on. Not to mention the very small ones right where you're about to enter the water - your feet will sink.The water was nice, the colors are fascinating indeed - amazing turquoise! But it gets pretty deep very shortly after you go into the water. Still, it should be visited and, of course, the picture you'd take will be great!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go early in the Summer
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Simply a beautiful beach..... we were advised to go early in the morning in order to get parked. We got there for around 9.00am and it was cool because the beach was in shadow. It quickly warmed up.We explored the cave and swam in the sea and saw lots of fish...... we even saw the little fish come to feed when the stones got moved. So glad we went here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely🥰
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I didnot have time to swim but seems to have no private beach facilities from above, lacking comfort. I cannot imagine myself lying on a towel on pebbles. I just passed by but the view was splendid.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach way down a long windy road. Water is a spectacular blue color. Nice beach, but can get crowded. Umbrellas and chairs available. One of the nicest settings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I've seen in my life. We stayed in Fiscardo and it took us 30 minutes to get there. The view from up the road leading to the beach is stunning, make sure to stop and take some pictures:)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach set within a cove. It is a pebble beach so remember shoes, on the plus side no sand in your shoes and clothes. The road down to the beach is great and view at the top of the cove are amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Suffice it to say Mirtos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are in Cephalonia, you should not miss this beauty.Long beach, beautiful turquoise, parking by the beach, should not miss it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not been to a better beach in my life. Could do with more sunbeds. The rocks instead of sand are bit painful as well. Take shoes!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: unreal view of the sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is impossible to describe in words that beauty.And that view creates huge expectations.In my case upon arrival to the island,we saw this beauty,it was unreal,like moment from dream.In September the 16th we came to Myrtos beach,the road just ok,parking big in front of the sea.White,fine pebbles ..turquoise blue sea of unreal blue ..perfect contrast blue-white..It was sunny,35 degrees.We had our umbrella,and you have to bring everuthing you need,because there is no cafe or restaurant on the beach.This beach is the most popular in Kefalonija,so it is must have here.We saw,for example,the buses that came all above the beach,for tourists only to experience that view.Be sure to check on Greek meteo the state of waves,because the big waves can spoil the pleasure(no smimming for example)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Late evening swim!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No matter where we go, each year at least a 4 days visit at Kefallonia is a must.  Each time the best swim takes place at Myrtos. Never at noon due to the extreme crowds and the burning rocks of the beach.  Ideal visit the beach late noon around 1700 and stay till dawn to check the sun fade away west. Very nice beach bar.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Astoundingly beautiful - best photographed from the top road
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I had read so much about Myrtos Beach before we arrived in Kefelonia that I was worried it would be a disappointment when we got there. Fear not! You will be absolutely knocked out by the colour of the water here. It sneaks up on you. We did it on a drive up to Fiskardo. The drive up that side of the coastline is spectacular. The water colour at the lookout point above Myrtos Beach really is exactly how it looks in those photos. They are not enhanced. We did not go swimming here so I can't comment on the notorious currents at the beach, nor the apparently difficult switchback road from the top of the mountain down to the beach. We did quite a switchback road down to Assos so if it is similar to that, it would be bearable. Do not miss this natural stunning beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning scenery and crystal clear water- late October visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the beach late October, therefore it was almost empty and absolutely beautiful. The sea was very calm and still warm, we didn't have any problem to get in and out of water like other people described. This almost deterred me from visiting, but I am glad we went. It was certainly worth the drive. We also didn't have water shoes, the pebbles in the water were quite small. On the beach they varied in size and after a few metres from the sea the beach turned sandy.  It is definitely worth a visit especially outside of main season.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blue and beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great overlooks from both sides of the beach. Fun switchback road down. Great spot for beautiful pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warm sand & sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Picked this beach to spend the day prior to late evening flight from the airport which is close at hand.Good parking under the pines. Free subeds, waiter service, clean, beatiful sand and very warm sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most beautiful beach in Greece!! Stunning view just in paradise! The waters are very deep so you need to be careful!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fab beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved this beach where you can walk for miles. Has a couple of restaurants that also serve cocktails. You can utilise some water sports on offer lay back and enjoy the music streamed out by the bars. The sunset was just breathtaking with a trumpet player blasting out popular songs whilst the sun set. Really magical so we went back for more!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning isn't appropriate
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is a 28 minute drive from ArgostoliIt is currently, still open, however, the lounge chairs have been removed and the restaurant, bar is closedSeveral folks are still sunbathing. Take your own beach chair or sit on the soft sandStop along the mountain road at the scenic lookout instead

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a stunning and gorgeous white sandy beach 🏖. Water is crystal clear and the views getting to the beach are amazing. Can totally understand why the local people are so proud of this location. I think the pictures speak for themselves 😍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Layered Blue Hues of Sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ah, what a scenic beach! The drive down the hill to the beach has lots of switchbacks, but taking it slowly gives passengers in the car plenty of viewing opportunities to the beach below. There's not a ton of parking, but we went a little later in the day so we found a spot. The beach is sandy...until you get closer to shore and then it's limestone so you should bring swim shoes. I wore closed Tevas and the rocks still found their way in making it really hard to walk. Limestone feels like quicksand so, between that and the bits of rock, if you aren't sure-footed to begin with, definitely bring a friend to help you get out of the surf. If I hadn't done that, I might still be there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven on earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Accessible by car. Crystal clear turquoise water. White pebbles. Warm & calm. Blessed experience.  Must do.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely amazing beach, tropical blue water, perfect for swimming! No sand but the pebbles underfoot are fairly soft at myrtos. Amazing scenery - such a beautiful place!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach soft sand clear water beautiful lovely bars and cafes on the beach, making our lazy days wonderful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove down the steep,hills with hair pin bends to the parking spaces, there were toilets and changing rooms, best take your own drinks and food, the refreshment area was closed. The beach looked beautiful from a distance, it was white pebbles, I found the sea drops off sharply, it was crystal clear, quite a heat trap ..... bliss

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picture Postcard Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Myrtos Beach at the end of the season so it was extremely quiet.The colour of the water is simply stunning, you definitely need to see this if you visit kefalonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breath taking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the most stunning views I have ever seen. An absolute must if you are on The island ❤️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: On the way to Assos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is just a beautiful beach. What a view from the watch point. Amazing colours and and great scenery

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach and water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This Beach is a must stop when travelling on Cephalonia. Beautiful beach and not so far by car from any place in Cephalonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the Nicest Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We traveled to Cephalonia after September 15 and for good reason. Small crowds. This beach can get quite crowded and parking is limited. The water a views are beautiful. Plan on renting an umbrella and two lounges for 10 euros. There are showers and dressing areas available. The restaurant was closed so I am guessing its seasonal.  Very important: Bring some water shoes. The beach is covered with beautiful smooth stones and its a lot easier to walk on with water shoes. The water was calm the day we were there but it could get a little rough. Another hint: When you come down the hill in your call there are several spots to take some photos. Do it. Also, stay to the right at the bottom and park on the beach right behind where all the umbrellas are. Very convenient to be able to have quick access to your car for clothes and food. Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful beach with turquoise sea, you do need beach shoes because of the pebbles. The sea was so clear it was great for swimming and snorkelling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beauty spot ruined by filthy people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and sea with toilet facilities sun beds and parasols water very rough tho and you need to keep your wits about you!On leaving beach we noticed people had emptied toilets in the parking area excrement sanitary towels and tampons along with wipes etc left everywhere disgusting no excuse

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mertos beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with few cafes etc careful of the undertows in the water they can be very powerful even at shallow depths, very steep twisting road down to the beach and of course back up to the top of the hill. Lovely place to spend a day, if you have a car bring your own food and water as will save you money cafes a little expensive great place worth a visit and great for pictures of the beach from the top of the hill and on the road to Assos looking back towards metros beach, kind of a must see once type of affair 😎

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This looks magical from the top of the road and once you drive down, the beach and sea are also amazing! Pebbles can hurt your feet a bit and would suggest going early (9-10am) as it gets super busy later and parking can be tricky.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having read the views of others as you do on TA, I was almost persuaded by some of the negative ones not to bother going. I'm so glad I cast them from my mind and went. It is without doubt one of the most beautiful sights I have seen. From the viewpoints above and on the beach itself. Beach not crowded, late September but 30° is hot enough, no issues with the winding road down to it with plenty of areas to pull in if needed. Crystal clear waters and good snorkelling at the northern end of the beach. Blown away by it, best one on Cephalonia for us but Antisammos comes a close second. Will go again before leaving.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice white (tourist) beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The colors of Myrthos, white rocks and bleu seas, are beautiful. There are some sunbeds and it’s nice to take pictures for holiday memories. Best place is the parkinglot at the mainroad. There are better beaches to visit, only thing is that these only can be reached by boat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Exhilarating views but!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views of the beach are breathtaking from up above and there is quite a nice beach but there is a very dangerous under current that takes you off your feet when trying to get out of the water and drags you back into the sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It is beautiful and perfect for snorkelling beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really enjoyed Myrtos beach . It was beautiful and relaxing beach . I also done some good snorkelling for beginners there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful from above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is lovely from above but considering it's one of the bigger tourist pulls on the island it's a little underwhelming once down by the sea. There are no facilities. The beach is of course completely stoney which is what makes the lovely colours but not very comfortable to sit on for any length of time. There is also a strong rip tide so caution for those swimming. Still very pretty though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love the film....had hoped to get to myrtos beach for some time. Well it was totally worth the drive from Skala. It is a visit I will never forget!! Paradise doesn't quite sum it up. Turquoise sea, shingle pebble beach-- please take sea shoes as very painful under the feet! Also be careful of the unpredictable waves as they knocked both me and my partner of our feet several times! Quiet and non commercialised unlike anti samos. You gotta go if you are on the island of Kefalonia!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Short visit to Myrtos Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited around 5pm on a pleasant afternoon and this seemed like a good time to avoid the crowds.The view from above the beach on the approach road is probably the best, as once we were on the beach we didn't consider it to be as stunning as we had been led to believe. Perhaps our expectations were too high.The approach road is quite untidy with a fair bit of graffiti and the beach itself is mostly pebbles with very little sand. The sea comes in with some force and is pretty impressive with its lovely blue colour, but I have been on much nicer beaches in other parts of the world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Electric Blues
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pictures don’t do justice to the views of Myrtos from the viewpoints on either side of the beach - quite simply breathtaking. The drive down the winding road is comfortable but parking is at a premium at busy times. The beach itself a mixture of sand and pebbles so beach shoes are advised. The view from the beach looking out to sea is one that will live long in the memory. The water itself is warm but cloudy due to the churn of the white rock. It also shelves quickly from the waters edge and you are very soon out of your depth. There is also a very strong rip when standing on the edge which can pull you in so be careful - confident swimmers will love the waves, less confident may find it a struggle. It is a “must see” when visiting the island if only from the viewpoints.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We saw the beach from the viewpoint on the main road where there is parking and you can take that famous photo of the beach easily. We did not have time to go down to the seaside and be there but it was enough for me to just look at it from afar and admire! Well worth seeing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach View
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My partner and I stopped off up on the road above for a view whilst on a holiday in Kefalonia. The view is absolutely stunning, especially if you have seen the Captain Corelli's Mandolin film. We didn't actually go down on the beach itself so can't comment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but disappointed with bar
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was one of the top recommended when researching for things to do in kefalonia. The beach is okay, clean and pebbly. I was a bit surprised that there was only one bar serving drinks and food and closed early at 5pm. The beach’s view point was much nicer in comparison ( pictures attached) Highly recommend the view point. Could skip the beach if necessary.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most amazing beach in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth the mountainous, scary roads to get there. It’s truly incredible. The violet light in the sky against the turquoise sea is astonishing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Realy great, but full of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the greatest beach we have visited on Kefalonia. But you must be aware of hundreds people coming here. It is better to go there early morning, or you will have to leave the car 0,5km up the road and go by yourself. It is full stony beach, so water shoes are necessary! Beautiful small cave is bonus to see here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visually stunning, amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow, perfect Turquoise sea, clear as clear can be, slightly tricky drive down but worth it, perfect white little stoney beach so beach shoes needed. If this beach view from the road above docent make you go wow then you're dead inside.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The online reviews raved about the 'best beach in Greece'. Well, I was underwelmed by what I found. Sure, the setting was impressive. A patch of sand between two high rock faces gave some nice photos, but the beach itself: too stony by half, not enough sand. The sea bottom sank away quickly and trying to make a dignified exit from the sea was impossible, as we 'oooh' and 'ouch'ed are way over the rocks climbing out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You have to be there!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Myrthos as part of a cruise tour!! What a beautiful beach!!! It’s water were transparent! Just spectacular!! The drive down the cliff was scary!!!! But sooo beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: MUST SEE! Perfect❤️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No words can describe this beauty. This is absolutely one od the best things to see on Kefalonia. Stunning!!! Watter is so clear.. and blue.. realy rare. What a beautiful nature..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Bay is truly a beautiful beach. It is covered with small pebbles (so bring shoes you can swim with) and incredible blue sea. There are some loungers and umbrellas to hire, but we bought our own parasol which was fine and meant you could get a bit further from everyone else (it can be a bit busy). The sea is clear and good for snorkelling, but we had been warned that there can be very strong currents so not to swim beyond your depth.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Be very careful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Myrtos last week. It was fine, gentle sea swam  & floated about with no problems. Went again today & totally different, the waves were bigger, nothing too dramatic if you’ve swum in cornwall, all was perfect until I tried to come out of the water. I am a confident swimmer, but the undertow & currents were so strong I didn’t know which was was up. If my partner hadn’t come to my rescue I honestly think I would have drowned. Please be cautious. The beach shelves steeply & the undertow is wicked. I feel lucky to be alive to write this. Warnings definitely needed here, lifeguards also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best seen from above.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An attraction that would be more popular if less people went there! Spoilt by remember of cars and wall to wall sunbeds.there are many more nicer beaches on Kefalonia. Driving down to,and back from this beach is a nightmare especially if you meet a bus going in the opposite direction.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous beach; difficult access!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this beach as part of a tour. The beach is stunningly beautiful, with crystal clear water, so great for swimming. The pebbles shelve away steeply though, so probably not as suitable for young children or less confident swimmers. The beach is mainly small pebbles, so jelly shoes or flip flops needed. Glad we weren’t driving down to the beach as the road is long, steep and full of hair pin bends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family day (half-day) on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely half-day on the beach with the family.  This was a repeat visit as we had come before in 2017.  Spectacular beach and cove when viewed from above or on the beach.  Get there early as the parking is limited and be careful how you park as a late arrival may block you in - a real pain if you want to leave before the crowds!  Tricky drive down and back up due to late arrivals parking on the access road.  Don't be deceived it looks like a really nice sandy beach but it is not, all stones I am afraid but water is fantastic.  Best improvement since 2017 is the opening of the taverna on the beach so you can get snacks and drinks there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach Vacation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I liked this place. It has a fee of ten Euros to use the chairs and umbrellas. I didn’t mind. You can bring your own. The waves were a lot of fun. We arrived at 11:30. Parking was crowded but worth the hassle. They had a small cafe there but I didn’t try it. They do offer parasailing if you want.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: parking is difficult but worth the walk if you have to park on the road further up and walk. Take jelly shoes as the pebbles are hot and difficult to walk on - stunning location and would recommend

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit but very pebbly!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did a little road trip today, Assos, Myrtos Beach and Fiskardo. We are stopping in Kateilos and hired a car. This is a "famous" beach and it looked beautiful from above. We ventured down. It's a nice beach but few things, very pebbly and I would suggest some of those water shoes cause even the sea was full of hard pebbles. Also, the showers could do with being a little close to the road, as, by the time you've washed the sand off you're stepping onto more sand to get off the beach and to the car.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do in Kefalonia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a day where there was no wind so the waves were not high. The scenery is beautiful, the water colors unbelievable but too wild for me to swim. I prefer calm shallow waters, definitely not for children.You can go for paragliding there where you go with an experienced person. I didnt do it but it must be a fantastic experience with such views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is just a lovely wonder to behold. The turquoise water and the lovely views all around. We took a taxi from the cruise port, which took about 40 minutes through a scenic ride. The ride too and from was just breathtaking. Definitely worth the time with plenty of photo opps along the way. We got there pretty early, around 9:30 am before the beach got too crowded. You can rent day beds and umbrellas for 10 Euros. There is also a bathroom facility and snack bar/restaurant right onsite. We stayed for about 4 hours. When we got there, we felt like we had the beach to ourselves. When we left, it was packed. It's definitely worth the drive to visit. The beach area is part sand and part small pebbles. I highly suggest you bring water shoes. It was painful to walk barefoot, and it is still full of small rocks when you get in the ocean. The water is truly beaufiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not what I expected!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When viewing from above just breathtaking.  When you are in the beach, not enjoyable, rocky beach I suggest water shoes, too many waves be careful with children.  If you arrive around noon you will park your car very high up the mountain, better to visit early morning or past 5

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just as beautiful as the photos. Whether you stop for the photo from above or spend some time on the beach, it's well worth it. In summer if you do spend time on the beach, arrive early, it gets busy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Soooo! Blue
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were driving up the coast to Asos when we stopped at the lookout overlooking Mytros beach. We were stunned at the incredible blue of the water and the white of the beach. I was positively idyllic. There was limited parking as it’s quite busy. Any beach lover would love a visit to Mytros.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The view and the water and simply amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a cab and arrived at 10:30 a.m and we prearranged a pick-up for 2:00 p.m which was just the right amount of time.  10 euros for a umbrella and there were plenty when we arrived.  Water shoes are a must (as the entry into the water is rocky). Taking pictures from the top is also a must.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go for the view not the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view from the top is amazing and definitely worth to go there but the beach is quite a let down with mediocre facilities and mucky waters with difficult entry and exit of the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must visit for sure. An amazing beach you rarely visit. Yes it is crowded. Yes you may have parking problems. BUT totally worth it. There is much space on the beach for your own umbrella so you dont have to wait in the private seabeds. Amazing blue colour combined with the rocks around and the sun. Just perfect.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but very busy with tourists - a victim of it's own beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a wonderful beach and the view from the top of the cliffs is fantastic. It's clean and lovely but unfortunately also discovered by coach loads of tourists. Best to go early or late and avoid the coaches

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views from the top of the mountain looking down on the bay are spectacular. The beach itself although pebbles has beautiful turquoise water and is a delight to swim in. There are simple facilities there which is good as it would take at least an hour to walk back up to the cafes at the top in the village. By 10.30 am the traffic down to the bay was heaving and there is no way I would have wanted to drive down to the bottom on a precipitous toad let alone trying to get back out of a disorganised parking system. We went on an organised tour with the excellent Avgerinos your company.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You HAVE to visit this beach if you come to Kefalonia.Great water, landscapes, even some small caves in the mountains around.The only BIG problem is the parking space. If you want to visit Myrthos you have to arrive there before 10 o'clock, else your car is gonna sit somewhere uptop, stranded on a cliff.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow I have never seen sea this colour. Absolutely stunning the drive down to the beach was scary and wAtching the coaches go up the hill was worth a watch. I would recommend A visit but be careful the waves are stronger than expected and may knock you off your feet. There is a bar and sun beds and clean toilets. Gets very busy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most amazing beach ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Besides the Maldives, i have never seen this kind of amazing blue in any other sea. Wonderful for swimming and the beach is clean, well organized with umbrellas, not noisy. I would recommend taking chips with you or a snack because they mainly serve drinks.Don’t miss to pass by the balcony to take a picture from the top.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An Experience That Must Seen First Hand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We first experienced Myrtos Beach from the cliffs above and knew it was a place that we had to visit... and when we did it didn't dissapoint, it's a beautiful jewel in Kefalonia's crown. The water has to be seen to be believed, now there are food and drink facilities down on the beach again the carpark and road get crazy busy but don't let that put you off go see for yourself.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a beach!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water is crystal clear. There is a beach bar in the area. Moreover there is a watersports area. The place is very famous but the access is difficult

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went later in the day (about 4pm) so it was a little quieter so got a car parking space and sunbed no problem. The beach is stunning and the water is a beautiful blue! definitely worth a visit. (Its a pebble beach so suggest you wear your flip flops down to the sea!)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous waters !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful beach! If you are driving (we hired a car) get there early to get a car park. beach chairs and umbrellas are available to hire on the beach for 10 Euro for 2 sun beds and umbrella! Take beach shoes as it is pretty rocky getting to water and in water. It is a large beach so plenty of space so you don’t feel on top of one another - loved this spot just gorgeous!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lovely beach ,but can get very busy .There are sun loungers on the beach, but you need to get there early . But be warned parking a car can be a nightmare and if no umbrellas ,can be very hot in mid summer .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but difficult parking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice clean water and space enough on the beach once you’re on it. During high season it can be difficult to park next to the beach and one has to drive up again to park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful places I’ve been
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is huge, calm water, rocks instead of sand. There’s a small cave in left side (left if looking to the sea) and I felt really sad about people be smoking inside. And smokers leaving cigarettes in the beach floor. If you are a smoker please watch yourself and don’t leave cigarettes on the floor wherever ! The most beautiful about this beach is the view from the road, there’s view points in left and right side of the beach...both views simply amazing. Parking can be a problem if you arrive after 10:00am during weekend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos is stunning. We went at about 6pm on the way back from Fiskardo to Skala. The waves were fun, it's pebbly so doesn't make for the most elegant exit from the sea! Lots of sun beds. It gets busy with parking but as we were there at the end of the day it wasn't an issue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best by boat
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, but SO crowded with disproportionate lack of facilities and parking. We drove in and straight out. Visit by private boat would be the learning. The ‘local’ tavernas are also underwhelming. As stunning beaches and way better eateries elsewhere. Great post card picture, reality not.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but go early!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach with crystal clear turquoise water. It's big enough that even in August it doesn't feel too packed. But def get there early (around 10am) to get a car space.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like a factory made cake!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We saw this beach recently on our drive up to Fiskardo. From the main road, the beach  is nothing short of spectacular. The white sand and cliffs with many shades of blue, create a vision which is so so special. I could see it was very busy with cars parked along the road leading down to it so we decided to visit it later on in the day. It was the right decision as we managed to drive all the way to the car park by the beach and park quickly and easily. However, my husband likened it to a ‘factory made cake’ which looks amazing but is a disappointment as you bite into it!!!! The beach was a dusty, dirty mix of pebbles and sand, which was more like builders sand, in fact , to me it seemed like a beach that had been extended by man! I do realise that for many families it’s clearly a popular beach, room to play and spread out, but after the massive wow factor looking down from above, I would suggest you look, then find somewhere further along the coast to relax and enjoy Kephalonia’s beautiful coastline!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is absolutely stunning.  It was busy, but worth it to see the clear waters.  It’s definitely worth a visit and is recommend going to Assos too that’s about 10 min drive further up the coast.The beach has toilets and a bar/cafe too

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very large and beautiful with a little cave on the left. There is a bar where you can buy sandwiches, icecreams, beverages. The beach is provided of umbrellas and sunbeds.The view of the sunset on the beach is breathtaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took photos from view point above. It was amazing,  the colours were stunning. Windy narrow roads,don't look down !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: bedazzled!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: prepare for some great waves!a water so blue and sand so white, it is no wonder this beach has made it to top 10.be careful with the waves, as there are strong currents and you can end up feeling as inside a washing machine. other than that, it is a must when in Kephalonia. nice place for sunsetyou can also enjoy paragliding there.Amazing view!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty view from afar
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gotta be prepared to park a bit far away from the beach which is annoying and exhausting but the beach is really pretty. During the afternoon when it became more calm, it was very dirty and  jelly fish were close by! Before it was crystal clear. There were no restaurants nearby, not really worth a second trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very crowded in the summer!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was stunning and the sea light turquoise, just as the pictures show, however they don't show just how crowded these stunning beaches are.  August is also the Greeks holiday time, so not only do you have the tourists from other countries trying to get to these stunning coves, but also the Greeks trying to enjoy their fabulous lslands.Not for us in the heat and height of summer - next time we come to Kefalonia, we will visit this gorgeous Island out of season.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best in Kefalonia!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For me is the best beach in Kefalonia, by far. I went there in August and It was easy to park the car and the beach has a lot of space (we had a lot os space for us). The water is hot and transparent. I recommend you to go to the viewpoint where you can take probably the best photos of your holidays! Incredible!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: August
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Immediately deep water not suitable for small children the road is dangerous and full of precipices.Not recommended in August the water is beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach  with turquise  watersIt has not many sunbeds and umbrelasThere ia a bar for drinks , snaks.....The most important problem is the parkingIt is a must - you should visit it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Natural beauty, but busy!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos is a fabulously beautiful beach and definitely worth a visit. The sea almost doesn’t look real with the white rock below reflecting through the water to turn it acquamarine.The drive down is fine until you get to the bottom, which is pretty congested. Better to leave the car on the side of the road and walk the last bit. The beach itself is large and pebbley with virtually no shade. There’s a small beach bar there too which is useful for drinks and snacks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a breathtakingly beautiful beach. Our family really enjoyed our time here and would advise getting here relatively early (by 10ish) in order to park easily and get great photos without too many others around. It’s a pebble beach, so rock shoes help we found. There are great views of the beach from the coastal road above to the North. When we left at 12, parking looked to be very difficult and the beach was pretty busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perilous narrow steep drive - horrific experience!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Drove all the way here from Skala and the imbeciles parking on the VERY narrow, thousands of metres high , steep road which goes on for over 2kms, made me so mad. You can’t turn round, and if afraid of heights you will be petrified. I am! The car drivers so selfishly park on this road that there are traffic jams on the way up and down and you are stuffed! They even park on the red markings which clearly say NO PARKING. This means inevitable traffic jams and no way of turning round. You will likely have a hire car, which is a different ball game to your own car and I didn’t like being so close to the edge on a steep incline as this is. It was so horrific that my car passengers freaked and I had to stop the car and get out. I had to ask another car driver - a French guy - to please turn my car round as I wasn’t going to head to the beach as it was too awful a drive. He literally did a ten point run for me which I didn’t have the nerve to do on such a thin road , and my car was literally clinging on the edge of the cliff with thousands of metres drop down. Terrifying!! How I drove up to the top of the road I will never know, with aggressive drivers on the way down seemingly not caring if your car went over the edge. I drove in first gear the whole way up. We did not regret not visiting the beach. There needs to be a better way of getting there than this!We went to a stunning beach just down from Agia Efimia instead!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sadly spoilt
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In the height of tourist season this beautiful beach of tiny white pebbles is best avoided...unfortunately! Unless of course you don't mind being rammed on with 100s of other tourists and having to park a mile away up a steep hill that is! Best viewed from the top road, take some photos and move on...in my opinion!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely big beach with amazing view and relaxing atmosphere. Very crowded if you come too late. Parking will be a problem after 9:30/10:00.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: To enjoy Myrtos in August stay away after 10 am
reviewsWithKeywords.text: August is a popular month for tourists. Myrtos is a breathtaking attraction for the hordes of tourists arriving by any means available (boat tours, buses, cars, bicycles ) and i am talking about HORDES of tourists. Despite the fact that the beach is long and wide, its literally INFESTED with people. The only “beach bar” that monopolises  the entire beach has queue of people waiting for a bottle of water  or coffee which sometimes exceeds 15-20’ waiting under the sun. Its CRAZY. My recommendation in order to enjoy this utterly magnificent beach is to bite the bullet and wake up EARLY . I mean EARLY so you can be at the beach the latest by 8.30am . During  this time of day one can feel that is in paradise. Calmness,space, quietness . True heaven.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach but....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunning from the lookout point - the blue hues are out of this world. It is also gorgeous from the ground. As for swimming, there are large and dangerous waves that hit against the shore and a very strong current pulling you in. People were getting pummelled by the waves (including me!). These are not nice waves that you can ride safely on a board or anything like that - they are dangerous! There is no lifeguard either. The locals said that the beach is like this 50% of the time, sometimes it can calm down in the afternoon. I would stay more than an hour here is the conditions are rough as this really isn’t a relaxing, swimming beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning view, may be very crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking scenery where the sea meets the mountain, with clear blue water. The beach it's long and large, with some sand and rocks. There are sunbeds and umbrellas. However near the water there are only pebbles and the entrance in water is very steep - 1 meter and you can't touch the bottom.Make sure to go early in the morning to catch a parking spot,  otherwise people are parking on the steepy slopes above the beach, more then 2km. We visited it on a Sunday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very crazy beach, no lifeguards
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s the most impressive beach with crazy waves I know. But nobody there is interested in healthy guests; there is no lifeguard, despite there are heavy waves. It’s more important how and wehre is your parking; for this controlling they have guyes.The stuff of the food-station is arrogant and unfriendly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but......
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The good: Myrtos beach is a beautiful beach. From high above, looking down onto it, it looks like a dream. The beach is made of beautiful white pebbles and sand. The water is warm and clean. It is a very large beach and gives the option of “ organized” meaning beach loungers and an umbrella and also bring your own umbrella and towels. It has one snack bar which was VERY BUSY but the employees managed to stay friendly and patient. There is a cabin that offers several bathrooms and even a few changing rooms and there are showers on the beach to rinse off the salt. There are also little taverns at the top of the road leading to the beach but I would suggest that you either eat before or after going to the beach. The not so good:The approach to the beach is a rather narrow 2 1/2 kilometer drive. In August, particularly during peak swimming hours, ( meaning morning until about 1:00) it is absolutely BLOCKED) with traffic. The first time we tried to go, there was a steam of cars coming UP from the beach telling us to turn back as there was “No Room” down below. We turned back and went another day but arrived about 3:30-4:00. The approach was open. The beach was still full and we stayed until 6:30. The day was still hot and the sun was still high. I recommend this strategy. General info:The “organized” part of the beach is quite a distance from the water.  There are plenty of chairs. I would recommend buying some “ water shoes”. This helps tremendously for pebble beaches. I would say that since this beach is so famous and is shown on many post cards and travel logs, you should go once but keep the information above in mind.  Also, I had a beautiful little butterfly land on my finger! Extra plus! ⛱😎

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Avoid this place. Just take a photo from top
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Driving down and trying to find a park on the edge of a steep cliff is like a nightmare. The place is packed with tourists. Save your time and check out a more exclusive beach nearby. Worth a snap from up the top only but drive down at your peril.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most beautiful picturesque beach i have ever visited, it was very busy, no available sunbeds but just sitting on our towels and swimming in clear water was fantastic....Don't forget your beach shoes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is really stunning and with sand and clean turquoise waters is certainly one of the most beautifull beaches in Kefalonia. But parking is very limited and you have to park on the roadside, at least a 20 minute climb away. Also tthe sunbeds and umbrellas are where when we arrived (10:30) almost  taken. Small bar for refreshments and food (sandwiches,  hotdog,  cheese pie). At 2 a clock there was no sandwiches and cheese pies.So, come early or do not come that all. Too busy in August.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach looks stunning from the cliff and is certainly one of the sandiest beaches in kefalonia. However parking is very limited and lots of people have to park on the steep roadside, at least a 20 minute climb away. There’s a refreshment bar there but with very long queues. Really wasn’t for us..... took one look and decided to leave that one and go elsewhere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing pebble beach in Cephalonia but 2 advices for you
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos beach was an amazing end to our excursion trip in  Argastoli the Cephalonia - Greece .. just be ready with you sun screen and beach shoes tight on your foot .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice photo op from the cliff, but dirty sea.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It looks beautiful from the road, white beach, blue water. So we stopped and went for a dip. The water was filthy with scum on top along the whole stretch of beach. In short take a photo and move on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning views on the way to this beach lovely village pass through , beach is amazing caves to explore very busy when we visited

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous but I prefer Lourdas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos beach is beautiful - from above! Nothing compares to the dramatic contrast of white cliff, blue sea, dazzling white sand. The beach itself is lovely but small, rather crowded and without many facilities. The drive there, with the inconsiderate car owners parking literally on the road on the way, is irritating. So worth a look but I am very glad I chose to stay someplace else as my “home base”.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: best beach to reach by car in Cephalonia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is no better beach you may reach by car in Cephalonia. Go in the morning, to get parking, at noon it's crowded. Get a good camera and make pictures from the road, from the beach, from everywhere. A drone for photos is a good idea too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking and unique!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have never swam in that shade of turquoise.,. pure magic! You have got to be there, no photo can ever capture the incredible colour of this water!! Paradise on Earth 🌎! Defiantly s ‘bucket-list’ item!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit but not a long stay!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely worth a visit to the view points to get the obligatory photo, but unfortunately, like most over touristy places, the beach had a lot of rubbish on it and in the water. Still nice to visit, but wouldn’t go out of your way!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos beach - the best beach ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such an amazing beach.  You must visit.  Amazing colour water and white sand.  Truly stunning.  Drive down to beach a bit hairy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: L...O...V...E...D  it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most stunning beaches I’ve been to and waters (other than those reachable only by boat) I’ve swam in. Yes, you can take a stunning, postcard perfect photo from above but to get the real feel of the beach one should really spend some time on it. Despite the pebbles the water is just stunning, and hiring a bed inexpensive (let’s not even compare it to France or the Amalfi Coast). The beach is enclosed in a bay like area, and the water very calm, making a long swim very enjoyable. A must visit when on the island!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pebbles and strong waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and picturesque so you can definately get you postcard picture especially from above but on the beach itself its all pebbles and rough on your feet so make sure you have shoes or sandles you can wear on the beach and in the sea. The waves can be quite big, the pull can be quite strong and it goes from shallow to deep within a meter or 2. Stayed here for about half an hour before deciding the waves and the pebbles were a little too much for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach Definitely worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, not too crowded as it’s larger than the smaller ones in the north of the island. Parking and access not a issue if you get there in the morning. Sandals required to walk over shingle. All the beaches are different, good to have lots of choices.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Average at best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Struggling to say very much positive about this beach. It’s not that it isn’t a beautiful beach but it’s so spoilt that the actual beauty of the beach pales into insignificance. If you enjoy sitting next to a very busy car park, listening to a man using a whistle to direct traffic one way, then this is the beach for you. Sadly for me, it detracted from what should be a stunning experience. The water was choppy and, in comparison to other beaches on the island, cold.  No desire to go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Only for short stay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Direction from Argostoli by bus to Divarta. The beautiful beach, which drives a minibus from Devarte, costs € 1.5.  Minibus travels several times during the day.  My recommendation is on the beach to arrive early in the morning or late afternoon.  Sunbeds and umbrellas are generally not free, and on the beach there is no cold.  It is best to come by car, swim, take photos, and continue on to Assos or Fiskardo.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unforgettable
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is really stunning, especially the view from the top. It really takes your breath away. In fact, the whole road to the beach is magnificent landscape. The beach itself is a mix between sand and pebble beach. The the water is so blue, that it is difficult to be described. So, you really have to visit it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Saw from the coastal road
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Didn’t stop but saw beach on way to assos. We were warned it’s not great for children as the sea is rough and bad undercurrents so be careful. It did look stunning from above. The coastal road is incredible but a little unnerving to say the least!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views - Choppy seas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited June 2018.Amazing beach and one of the best photos I have ever taken from the coast road, however on the day we visited the sea was very rough and for a weak swimmer like me a little intimidating. Seems like when you get into the water the ground drops off quite steeply but that might just be the way I felt as per above. Saying that, it is very beautiful and a must see if you are on Kefalonia. When we visited there were no sun beds or life guards and the toilet facilities were portoloos but as said, amazing place to visit and the drive down to the beach pretty spectacular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The position and the view of the beach from high is perfect. The color of water is very beautiful. It has sunbeds but there is enough space if you want to seat down with your own umbrella and enjoy the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning panoramic view from top
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most stunning beaches when you view it from above. The white pebbles against the turquoise see is breathtaking. However, you will need to park quite a way up the hill as it is very popular. Very few sun beds and parasols available so make sure you bring your own. Lying on huge pebbles is Not comfortable. The sea is quite cold here and getting in and out of the sea tricky due to the pebbles. Definit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top 20 beach in the world, really?!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The overwhelming consensus was, no. Don’t get me wrong it’s very picturesque, providing you ignore the car park and the winding snake of cars disappearing  up the hill. 2 Sun beds with a brolly will set you back €10, which is a little higher than what we’ve experienced elsewhere. There is somewhere to change which was clean and tidy. We didn’t use the toilets, so unfortunately I can’t give you any insight there. There are also showers to wash the salt off after a dip. The sea is cold, much colder than at Antisamos. Also the waves are much more significant, so not really suitable for young children. The drive there, as with many roads on the island will keep you on your toes. I’m sure the views are amazing from the road but my focus was 100% on the thin strip of tarmac. There is one bar at the beach, we didn’t use but was very busy.After having had a super swim we left after 2 hours. There isn’t anything else to do. Oh, don’t forget your swim shoes, the beach is pebbly and you’ll regret not having them. In summary, nice to visit, I’d get there early as parking can be a challenge (especially if you are unfortunate enough to need to park on the hill). Glad we went, but are we going back? No, we prefer Antisamos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wasps and strong undercurrents...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have visited Myrtos Beach many times and it's one of my favourite beaches in the entire world but this year there have been many unfortunate incidents on the beach and in the sea. There are wasp warnings, so if you're allergic, be sure to have your meds with you. There are no life guards on the beach this year, no first aid kits, nothing! In June, a woman died on the beach after being stung. The sea is also really dangerous, as there are very strong undercurrents that pull you under, so don't let your small kids swim alone. There have been a few reports of people almost drowning this year. So, if I were you, take photos of this stunning beach but avoid spending time on it. There are so many other beautiful beaches on the island that are exquisite and safe to swim at.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Myrtos beach on the same day as Melissani Cave and I recommend both! Crystal clear water and a very large beach with a lot of room

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but way too crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Myrtos Beach is a genuine beauty, which became way too touristy, which kills its magic. After 12:00 it is absolutely impossible to park. The cars are abandoned along already narrow and treaky road, which makes the trip simply stressful and dangerous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, a must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach with clear turquoise water and white pebbles. Umbrella / beach bed rentals available and a small café. Don't forget to swim through the small cave and jump from the big rock at the far left of the beach (if you are facing the ocean). Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The road is steep and narrow to the beach, however it is worth the effort. We arrived around 6pm on a warm June day and it was beautiful and reasonably quite.We did not want to leave.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A real eye cather
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s lovely to see such treasure but almost impossible to swim when the waves are present which happens quite often because of the wind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing setting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is worth a visit,  it is set against huge dramatic cliffs and the water is turquoise clear, but this place doesn’t have good facilities “ time for a make over” the beach it self is made from white pebbles which are very painful to walk on when leaving the water 😫 I recommend beach shoes to mitigate the pain and getting in the water is quite difficult as the waves roll in... moan over, it’s worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Outstanding beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Got to be of the most beautiful places I’ve ever seen, crystal clear water and breath taking views. It’s such a pity that to get there was so frustrating. My only fault on the trip was the road down to was manic with cars and buses trying to get up and down, nowhere to park once you start your descend down only to drive back up frustrated. Advice is to park at top of hill and walk down but prepare for the half mile gruelling walk back up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tips for parking - and don’t be duped by fake parking attendants
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Beach is lovely and if you are on Kefalonia, it is worth the effort to spend half a day there - best early morning. With parking, the best advice is to go early - before 10am. Parking signage is minimal and possibly confusing when you first arrive. After the last hairpin bend, not far above the sand, you come to the apex of a triangle which has a small bus shelter - you need to go straight ahead / slightly angled to the right - as this takes you onto the triangle which is effectively a one-way street, and allows cars to go in an anti clockwise direction around the triangle, back up to the bus shelter, and out of the beach. If you arrive after 10am you are probably going to have to park up on the hairpin bends. You generally have to drive all the way down to the sand, around the triangle, and then back up to park in the next available spot up the hairpins. You have to park on the right side of the road as you go up. Whatever you do, don’t be duped be duped by fake parking attendants - these will encourage you to park in the wrong spot, ask you for money, and you will generally be in for a disagreeable time. (We saw this exact thing happen to 3 unsuspecting tourists, who were just trying to do the right thing). Be warned.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth to visit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go there by 9am and choose your spot.2 sun beds +umbrella 10euro.Most of the things at the bar coast 3euro ,bar opens by 11am.Free showers,WC and parking.Crystal clear water. Great place to be!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most Famous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking view from up to the beach. Beach has white stones and sand , has sunbeds and beach bar. Water is blue but not very clear, not good for snorgeling, going deep imidietly. Amazing to watch  sunset there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Park on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Back in 2015 my late husband & I took a shipment of goats from the UK to Greece. Some went to the mainland and the rest went to Kefalonia. We went by ferry from the mainland with our livestock trailer. After delivery we were free to explore. Having seen Myrtos Beach in the famous "Captain Corelli's Mandolin" film we set off to find it. What a stunning location. You can drive down a steep track all the way to the lovely beach. My husband had his last swim in the sea there so it is a very special place for me.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking view  when driving down to beach.  Colours of the water fantastic.  Sand and pebbles strongish current and very very  hot down there   bar and toilets at back of beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magical Myrtos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Famous for 'that' film but this beach has more to offer than that. Beautifully blue waters and a long white pebble beach. A great place to sit back, relax and enjoy listening to the waves crashing into the beach. Parking can be chaotic so get there early or late on and walk further down the beach towards the cliff to escape the crowds. Oh, and don't forget to get a picture at the top of the cliffs on the way to or from the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow wow wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos beach is in Pylaros and  is surrounded by tall and green cliffs. The color of the sea changes from dark blue to electric blue and turquoise. Its  stunning at every moment of the day.You cant help but be captivated by this location. It just draws you in. This is not a beach to go swimming in. The current is extremely dangerous. I have never seen such huge waves. The day I visited no one was swimming, instead all were at the edge running into and quickly away from the waves crashing around. Definitely keep an eagle eye on young children. To rent a chaise longe for the day is 20 euros. We had good cocktails and very friendly service from the staff at the only bar there. The beach toilets were clean.A must for anyone in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful to look at .... great water temp... take shoes.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos is a MUST SEE if you're in the area. You really can't be close and NOT go. Be aware of sitting in the natural shade provided by the 'mountain' as the rockfall is pretty hectic. If windy don't put up umbrella. The water is lovely - the pebble beach can be pretty rough on your feet so if you have water shoes take them. It's a beautiful beach to look at and apparently is open to topless bathing and on the right-hand-side apparently nudity... I saw 3 women topless and no nudity. Very kid friendly and family friendly. Go early to avoid the crowd and also it gets SUPER hot after 2 so the earlier the better. Enjoy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turquoise Blue
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach- the colour of the water is breathtaking(we were told the amazing colour of the water is due to limestone).A strong current &  waves strong enough to knock you over the day we went.Quite a journey around & down by car (we took a taxi!)On the rocky beaches I would recommend the swim shoes you see for sale around the place (around €10 Euros).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just do this all day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of if not the most beautiful beaches I have been to. Limited bathroom/changing stations so come in your bathing suits. Additionally there is no restaurants or snack stands so bring lunch or snack with you. Wide open beach with no shade bring umbrella  if you so desire. Plan to spend all day at the beach. Can taxi back and forth from the port.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Drove to this beach on moped, stunning views from above, white pebble beach with Crystal clear water, a must to see when in Kefalonia

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not as good from beach level as from above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely stunning when viewing from above, so picturesque. Given its beauty it attracts lots of visitors. Beach was very busy and dirty. Couldn't relax as you're likely to get a wind glider land on you as they use this beach to land on after jumping from cliffs above. The sea was rough when we visited and got deep quickly. Much better beaches around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach, beautiful setting, great view and journey to there.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Yes, this is the most famous beach and for good reason. The journey to there is incredible and the view is stunning but you need to be a confident driver and not have fear of height (like everywhere  else in kafelonia). We personally prefer anti Samos near sami but still very good, get water shoes or crocs, the pebble beach will be hard on your feet

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dramatic beach landscape
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Turquoise waters, small white pebbles underfoot. Gets deep very quickly. Take a parasol (or hire a lounger) as there's no natural shade from the punishing Greek sun. We had 2 dips and got out before we fried to death.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were told its a very photographic place and indeed it is.  The small white pebbles that make up the beach glisten and glow in the sun.  Views from the top are simply amazing.  You do not have to be a photographer to obtain good pictures.  Well worth seeing and definately on a list for those wanting scenic views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach is what you need to see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Beach is what you need to see .We have seen it and it is true . We believe it may be one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe . The colors are unbelievable !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I liked Myrtos because it is a stunning location with picturesque white rock beach and a great cave to explore on the south side. We set up our beach towels against the cliffside so we could be shaded from the sun and swam in the clear blue waters. The temp is perfect and like the rest of the waters around kefalonia I never needed to buy goggles because I could see just fine with my eyes open in the clear waters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Be aware of the falling rocks!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Looking for a shade I spent the most of the day on the very left side of the beach (sea wiev left side). I was lucky not to get injured by a heavy rock falling from above. The stones are falling the whole day long and there is no sign. If you want to be in shade, move deeper into a cave

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely awesome setting one of the nicest beaches we have seen on our holiday so far beautiful sand crystal clear azure blue water parking is limited a couple of tavernas and toilets showers too

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
