reviewsWithKeywords.text: Would recommend but you'll have to endure a hassle to experience what is indeed an amazing beach. As usual, beautiful things attract big crowds. The municipality in Kefalonia needs to do a much better job organizing access/parking and amenities (overall, the worst experiences we had in the wonderful island of Kefalonia were due to the local authorities not doing or being terrible in doing things that elsewhere would be taken for granted - reinforced my belief that if you want to destroy something beautiful, give it to incompetent/indifferent public servants, especially at the local level).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I wouldn't say this is the best beach on Kafelonia but the colours of the waters and the scenery even on a cloudy day are exceptional. Swimming is a no go as the sea current is strong but you're simply there to take in the ambience and the experience of visiting a glorious natural beach which doesn't require any kind of commercialism or ammenties.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is truly an amazing beach, beautiful turquoise color and very clean  surroundings. if you have children it s not so great as there are no basic amenities. We were lucky as the day we visited they put some umbrellas so there was some shade however there are no toilets and you have to go all the way to the village .I know the beauty of this place  remains in the unspoiled nature  so maybe toilets are not the best idea however something must be done.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best looking water I saw on the island worth the drive and hassle for a parking spot. If you are driving by car get in early or prepare to walk 10minutes down the road and walk. There isn’t much at the beach other than toilets & a man offering hang gliding for 60€ plus 20€ if you want the video. Worth a visit if your a beach fan or want some amazing selfies

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning location but does not fully deliver
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So this Beach was on the "Must do" list after all the hype and Captain Corelli's mandolin.... This is a stunning beach to view from above, look for some of the viewpoints on the mountain road above and it will take your breath away. But as a beach for swimming, especially with a young family then please beware. The beach is a "natural" beach, there are no real facilities. The stones, although rounded, are very hard on your feet, you do need foot protection and the waters are very strong. The water drops off very deep in only a few metres and on the day we visited the normally crystal clear Kefalonia waters were very "milky", snorkelling was a waste of time. I am not sure younger ones would really enjoy this beach, they would need very close monitoring if swimming, cannot build sandcastles and have limited access to toilet facilities. Overall it is a must visit location but if staying a long time take something comfortable to lay on !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you go to Kefalonia then make sure you visit Myrtos beach.  There’s a narrowish winding road down to the beach.  There is limited parking at the bottom.  I’m sure during the day it’s hellish busy with vehicles.  We went just before sunset to watch it setting and it was fairly empty, just about 2 dozen people on the beach doing the same as us.  The sea is a magnificent blue colour that’s makes for fantastic photos.  Waves can be high and there is a drop off about 3 meters out in the water.  The pebbled beach is stunning and surrounded by high cliffs.  Great place to chill and watch the sun set.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Deep blue waters in a remote location. On a windy day the waves can go really nasty. Definitely a place to see in Kefalonia

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunningly Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you come over the ridge and see that water for the first time you will add this to your list of favorite places on earth.  I am not a huge beach person, but I could not wait to get into that water.  No one photograph can actually capture the real color of that water.  Breathtaking and refreshing.  If you are on Cephalonia, you must visit here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but not organised
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breathtaking views and clear blue waters. The pebbles make it difficult to get in and out of water. It also deepens in 3 m and the fact that it is not organised makes it difficult for families with small children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular beach - though better for photos than sitting on!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos really is a stunning looking beach with the colour of the water taking your breath away.  The views from the coastal road are amazing.  We drove down the windy road to the beach one day during our stay in early June and it still looks amazing close up with beautiful blue water, however there are no sunbeds and the stones are a bit tricky to negotiate in and out of the water.  I am not a great fan of lines of sunbeds on a beach, however it is a little strange that the most iconic beach on the island has so few facilities. There is a blue building in the middle of the beach but no sign of it being a taverna or providing toilet facilities or sunbeds.  If it is not in use then it does detract from the overall beauty of the place.  Maybe we were a little early in the year and these are provided in high season only.  In any case it remains a must visit beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Most Beautiful Beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach.  the water is very rough for swimming.  You will need shoes for the rocks in the water,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This large beach and its beautiful blue waters was in my opinion the best place in Kefalonia. Although the water is quite wavy at times, one can enjoy the beach pretty well. Also, the sights from above are spectacular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most famous beach in Kefalonia. It features in all the advertising for the island. It is truly stunning. However, there is a downside to this beach. At times it does have a dangerous rip tide/current that can sweep you out to sea. Swimmers be careful. If unsure, get advice before heading to this beach to ensure you can enjoy it to its best.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: myrtos beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super view! Very clear beach.One of the best in Europe.You must visit if you are in kefalonia!  Be careful the waves!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disapointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My family and I visited the beach today. We were so excited to go there since all the reviews we read say it’s worth it.When we arrived there we were very disappointed. The water was blue but dirty, no sun beds or bars.That was ok i mean every beach is dirty once in a while. The most disturbing thing i saw was some drunk persons behaving very irresponsible.Over all, i can say that the beach is beautiful only from far away, since the close up is disappointing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful clean water - worth the drive down
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were stating close to Myrtos beach so had to visit. We had seen it on our way to our villa from the coastal road and from this height you can see the clear turquoise water really clearly. The road down to the beach is a bit hairy, very steep and twisty with blind bends and a real drop in height from the top but I managed it. There's no cover on the beach, parasols or sunbeds, not sure why and it's pebbly so difficult to walk on but the water is so clear and refreshing (and deep). I imagine if you were there early or late and had it to yourself it would be magical. Everyone talks about seeing the sunset at Myrtos which I imagine is spectacular, but I wasn't going to wait for dark to make the return trip back up that road!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From above looks amazing,when u go down is even better..the deep blue and the amazing water is something unique.lovely

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most turquoise water to be found on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myself and my partner visited after hiring a car, as we had been told by reps and other people its the best beach on the island. When we drove the views were breathtaking, even on a slightly cloudy day. However, I couldn't agree more that its nicer to look at than be on. I found no problem parking but the beach is pebbly and quite littered to be honest. Such a shame people cant look after it as there are huge bins provided by the car park. I stayed here for an hour or two then moved on. Although a stunning beach I spent my afternoons on far nicer beaches which were more quaint and unspoiled.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best viewed from above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the most beautiful beaches I’ve ever seen. From above. We descended the windy road to take us down and were waved on by a parking attendant even though we’d found a free spot behind some other cars not far from the bottom. We then sat in a queue for 10 minutes while people struggled to get in and out of 2 car parks.Once we finally found our way through and into a space we headed towards the water. What looks like white sand is actually tiny white pebbles, something like you might find in a builders yard. They get in your shoes and in between your toes and hurt your feet. We put our towels down as there are no sun beds available, and walked towards the water over big white pebbles.Getting in wasn’t easy. It was painful walking over stones of different sizes. One we got in, the water was lovely. Not clear, but warm and refreshing, but it got deep very quickly.Getting out was even harder. We worked our way to the shore on our bellies and made a few attempts at climbing out without being pulled back in, then over the hurty stones and pebbles and back to our towels. We only went in twice and we won’t be going back again.  This beach is definitely best viewed from above!As it’s so famous in Kefalonia and all the guidebooks recommend a visit, there really ought to be more facilities. There are no beds/umbrellas, no toilets and nowhere to buy food. And the parking needs organising. But it you like things unspoilt, you’ll love this!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice swim
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited today. We arrived at 8:30 and we had the place to ourselves. The beach is pebbly as is the entry / exit to the sea so it is quite hard and difficult to walk on in bare feet. Sea shoes are a must. The water was lovely and warm and we really enjoyed swimming here. Very limited facilities. We left at 9:30 as we just stopped for a quick visit and it was starting to get really busy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clear waters and nice surroundings
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visted Myrthos beach yesterday,a beach that you cannot miss if your in kefalonia. Waves are a little bit stronge, so families with small kids should keep eye on them.The surrounding cliffs that surround the beach and the Crystal clear sea are awesome. One thing I didn't like was the huge amount of cars rushing down to find a parking and not giving chance others to drive out, so at some point you can be stuck with moving. Still is worth visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Take supplies!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came to myrtos beach this morning...such a beautiful spot and the views are spectacular. However there are no sun loungers to hire and no beach bar,other than in the bars up the hill.Toilet facilities not great either..So make sure you're prepared!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach and the adjoining cliff are beautiful. Must visit for a sunset or sunrise. But the waves are harsh so experienced swimmers only. The color of the water is immersive and there is a small cave hidden towards one end of the beach, needs caution due to the waves. No restaurants or umbrellas though, get your own stuff

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful long beach, unfortunately the sea was rough so we couldn't swim and my son lost his face mask, so be careful, the waves are stronger than you think. Pebbles no sand so it's good to have the rock shoes. There is no place to buy water so make sure you have it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wednesday on the Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were advised that this was a must do trip ! Hired a car and went for the day One of the most beautiful beaches and sea to swim in ! You need an umbrella as it was baking hotAlso although lots of parking it looked liked madness after about 1130 ! And you need a cool box with drinks and sandwiches as nothing on the beach itself but tavernas up in the village

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the best beach on the island. A big beach with soft little pebbles. The water is amazing. It’s turquoise and very warm

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Viewed from road above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We only view this beach from the road above as we were on a coach trip and coaches can’t get down.  It looked spectacular and our tour guides told us the beach is made up of very fine stone, almost as fine as sand, but the sea gets deep very quickly

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but blustery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a view, what a beautiful setting, I’ll even allow the stones. With a few patches of sand here and there, it would’ve been perfect. The sea was amazing, so clear, so blue and the windy conditions made it a lot of fun for our little boy who thoroughly enjoyed being swept out by the huge waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breath taking place. So beautiful. The views from the top are stunning and once down the beach is gorgeous. Sandy and white pebbles and the bluest sea. There is a small cafe and changing area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well worth a visit , stunning blue waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Myrtis beach today and thought it was stunning. The setting is awesome. The kids had great time with the big waves which were crashing in. Couple of suggestions if you plan to visit :1. The drive down is pretty steep and can be very tight especially when it’s busy, worth being early to avoid any hassle. We arrived at 1pm and it was chaotic at the bottom where cars were parked and others trying to leave.2. There are no Tavernas or bars down there so make sure you have water / lunch with you. We didn’t and ended up heading back up to one of the Tavernas at the top of the road ( at the junction ).3. There are some sandy parts to the beach but it’s pebbles when you try to get into the water. If you don’t have the swim shoes , you can look like a bit of an idiot ( as I have ) trying to walk on the pebbles. It is uncomfortable, I plan to spend the 9 euros on a pair of these things tomorrow.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bit exposed and choppy, but impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Aesthetic surroundings , but you need to choose your day if you enjoy swimming in crystal clear calm seas. The day we went had quite impressive waves crashing on the shore which is good fun for adults and strong swimmers, but limited fun for sub-teenagers who may object to being tossed about onto the stones by the forces of nature.Watch out for paragliders landing on the beach. No immediate facilities for refreshments or loungers. Don't fancy being here during next earthquake!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not as nice as it looks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: From the viewing points, you are like WOW!!! It looks so beautiful and bright blue. Everyone is taking photos outside of their cars. But you get down there, there's hardly any car park spaces but we found one in the end. It's a stone beach which is fine as the lovely beach in Sami is the same and we loved that. But this beach doesn't look as clean as the one in Sami. There's no sunbeds so you need to pay on the towel on the big stones which dig in your back and isn't nice when your pregnant. Then the waves!! They are so big and aggressive that my husband went in and got pushed all over the place and big rocks under the sea rolling over and hitting his legs. He cut both of his ankles and he was even wearing his swimming shoes. It wasn't safe for me to get in so we left after an hour so did loads of other people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turquoise sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You will need a car to visit. Take some provisions with you as when we went in June there was no beach bar open. The sea was rough when when we went but great fun.It is the most turquoise sea you will ever see especially when viewed from the mountain road above.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We want to see this beach because of the film.We weren't intending to drive down as thought we would just view from above ? We were glad we took wrong road and ended up on the beach . Lovely to walk along not a lot of people there the time we went ? And a nice paddle in the water ,so we could say we'ed done it.Didn't try the toilets though as had read awfull reports about them ?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blown away by the beauty of this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Myrtos Beach today for the first time and was absolutely blown away. Such a beautiful place.The drive down to the beach is very windy (probably and understatement!) there are areas that you can pull over and stop to take pictures.The beach itself is white pebbles and the sea is different shades of turquoise and so warm.If you plan on staying a whole day take supplies with you - ice box, food, drinks, umbrella.Can't wait to spend time here again - outstanding.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful. Amazing colour of the water and not too crowded! It is recommended to go there by car since it is quite a hike to walk back up after the swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The colour and feel of the water are both beautiful. The temperature of the water is nice. The beach is picturesque. It is a pebble beach so if bare foot it hurts. Plan on visiting for an hour or two. It is too bare to remain all day. Bring a sun umbrella as there is absolutely no shade.Recommend going for a swim and then heading for lunch in the nearby town. A touch and go kind of stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Greece in one picture
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A real must to actually see the scene that makes Kefalonia stand out from the rest then you have to do this one. The road has now been rebuilt above this idyllic view and in the process they have put in a viewing point above Myrtos Beach to allow you to take the picture that you will see on many brochures. Then make your way down the twists and turns to the beautiful white stone beach and have a sunbathe. Be careful though as the heat can become excessive as you are within a sheltered bay and a parasol is advisable if you plan to stay any length of time. A real must and have visited this location many times over the years.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picture postcard
reviewsWithKeywords.text: looks amazing from the view point, a must stop if driving to Asso or Fiskardo. We didn't drive down but you ca npark near the beach but it gets busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning and isolated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely lovely beach with spectacular views from the high approach, be advised quite a away from anything else so take everything you need if at all possible. I mean food, drinks and Sun protection including a sun umbrella if possible. I am not sure I would take children to this beach as it is a steep path down and no other attractions other than sand, beautiful clear water and the views. If you go you want to make it worth it - so I would allow more than three hours if not all day. No photos included in review it's one of those places you have to see for your self!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice views, but beach not well looked after
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We'd read that this was amongst the best beaches in Greece, but I'd have to disagree. The best part were the really amazing views of the beach and bay for the hills above. No doubt that they were amongst the finest in the land. But the beach itself was poor, chaotic and small parking area, few facilities on the beach, so nowhere to get a drink etc. There seemed to have been something there in the past, as there were unsightly ruins of earlier shacks, or that is what it looked like. Pity, it could have been so nice. Anyway, if you like a white pebble beach in a scenic cove, and you bring your on food and drink and anything else you need, then it's fine. I just think there are better beaches around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning water - pebbly beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We used a car to get here. We got lucky with parking. We arrived at 1pm, the beach was busy but never crammed. Unless you have leather feet you need to get some aqua shoes as the pebbles are excruciating. I had mine with me but thought I would give it a go as I spend most of my time (when not at work with no shoes on) alas it was hell and on went the aqua shoes. The beach drops away quickly so it only takes a few metres and you can’t touch the bottom. I’m 1.76m so definitely not short. Water was beautiful, clear and very warm towards the surface. Very insta-worthy. There are toilets and open beach showers to rinse off but that is it. BYO everything. Saying that, and being an Aussie. I still prefer the soft sand and equally clear water at Lourdata.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Beach is a beautiful pebbled beach with clear blue waters. I would recommend beach shoes if you plan to go in to the water and sun cream as the beach is a real sun trap. You definitely need a car to visit and parking is limited on busy days.There are no beach side bars or restaurants so taking your own drinks and food is advisable.The view is amazing as you come down the mountain towards the beach and the beach is pure heaven! Enjoy :-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Island tour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful colours, what an amazing beach a must see for anyone visiting Kefalonia, only go into water if you are a very strong swimmer

reviewsWithKeywords.title: toilets fit for animals so dirty they are
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach with no toilet facilities at all. two loos so dirty that I don't see how people can use that beack

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love it - but take shade!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its not yet commercialised so nowhere to change, eat or have a pee, no sunbeds, no shade - but if you just want turquoise warm seas and a lovely picturesque beach - its Myrtos.  We LOVED it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tourists Must
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had to see this beach as it is very much spoken of.  Especially, since the film Captain Corelli's Mandolin.The view from the viewing points at the top are spectacular and it was a compulsion for me to take the ride down to the bottom and walk or paddle on this beach.  When I arrived at the beach instead of beautiful sands it was intact very fine shingle.Getting into the water was fine but when I tried to get out my feet sunk into the shingle and trapped my foot which made it difficult to get out without resorting to a very undignified crawl on all fours. The water seemed not  to want me to leave.All in all the illusion I saw from reviewing point at the top was disappointing on the ground so to speak.Better to see from above and enjoy the view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Beach is a must see when visiting Kefalonia. We were lucky to spend the day on a private 4x4 tour island tour and stopped at both sides of the beach to capture the views. It’s just stunning. We drove down the road to have a walk on the beach. The beach is not sandy, it’s small pebbles so it can be quite uncomfortable on your feet. Only problem for us is that there is no shade, you have to take your own beach brolley and if you are visiting for the day, you would have to purchase one. The only facilities are toilets however there are a number of tavernas and shops at the top of the hill. Again, another must see if you are visiting the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach & gorgeous clear water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the top 10 beaches. Amazing beach and clear water... the view from above and in the water looking back to the beach is fantastic. In June we had to take our own umbrellas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: NICE BEACH but not spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A ''postcard'' vista greets you when you first turn up and after a long-ish drop down the hairpins you arrive at the Car Park which was ok for when we were there but I'd guess gets full up peak season.Mostly Limestone coarse sand / shingle / stones there's a cave worth looking at to the southern end which you can walk  /swim under.NO facilities to eat [ they are back up the beach access road about 3/4 mile climb away ] but there are Loo's in a block on the beach itself.No loungers or Umbrellas etc. Its simply a beach and the 'drop off' means the 'tots' might need a close eye on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: W didn't go down onto the beach but it is well worth going to the two viewpoints and looking at it from above. The colour of the sea against the beach is spectacular!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic view but in reality - shocking!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views of this beach are spectacular but after going all the way down to the actual beach we were disgusted. There are no facilities to buy anything (water, snacks etc) but the main fault for us was the disgusting toilets that clearly had not been cleaned for some time. Needless to say after travelling for over an hour tosee this place and leave after a couple of minutes we were extremely disappointed.  CLEAN THE PLACE UP!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely breathtaking!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Be sure to see Myrtos Beach!Whether from high above the cliffs or down to the beach itself you'll be enchanted!It's got this 'wild' and 'raw' beauty to it!It comes as no surprise that just a few years ago it  gained the gold award as the most beautiful beach in Europe and in another worldwide contest it came third!The road down to the beach is unfortunately not that ideal...there are so many curves and turnings and the cliffs above do give you the 'chills' when your mind goes to slidings of rocks and so on which is quite frequent at the sides of the beach...On the other hand if you intend to swim there and you have small children I'd say don't let them go deep especially if there are waves.Maybe at the edge the waters are shallow but from one moment to the other you could find yourself in sudden depth.The white sand which is full of pebbles adds this uniqueness to the whole picturesque scenery!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Looked nice from up above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped here for photos as part of a tour of the island.  The view from high up was pretty amazing, lovely colours reflected in the sea and it looked idyllic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's a beach......
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pleasant beach with clear waters. Safe for bathing. Good views from above on the map road. Good sunset snaps.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Myrtis beach. Beautiful sea but white stones not sand. Popular area to visit . Either go by tour or by hiring a car which we did. Not easy to walk if disabled. But a beautiful view from the road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful part of Kefalonia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I agree with other reviews that the view from above Myrtos beach is the most stunning, however there is nothing like actually walking on one of the most beautiful places in Kefalonia.Our visit was at the end of the day as the sun was sinking over the sea. There was still some warmth in the sun and the colour of the azure sea against the white pebbles/ stones was beautiful.It was quiet and we parked on the back of the beach. Reading some of the reviews regarding the toilets takes away the main reason for visiting this beach. It’s beauty.It is humans that create the dirty toilets and nature that creates Myrtos beach. We spent a few minutes on the way back to our car picking up litter and mess left by other visitors to help keep this area clean.Don’t worry about toilets and score the area one star. Sit on one of the large white rocks, look up and down the beach then stare out to sea and thank god that you are still alive to enjoy it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Toilets a disgrace 2
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach looks like paradise. We just wanted to change but the toilets were disgusting, truly horrible. We left . Don't go, just look at it from above and enjoy the beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in the world!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos beach has an amazing view! It's the most famous sight of Kefalonia, one of the best beaches in the world and you must take a swim there! Be careful because it can be too wavy and even dangerous deep when it's very windy!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Toilets a disgrace
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and views on walk down to it but toilet facilities not acceptable and spoiled what could have been a good experience.  Cave was worth a visit, easy to access and room to stand up in. Lovely white pebbles and sand and someone had made some interesting sculptures from the pebbles which were really cool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Idyllic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The pictures of this beach don't lie. The view from the road above highlights the contrast between aquamarine blue sea and brilliant white beach which is pebbly rather than sandy. Free Car parking is available at beach level but take your own sunshades and drinks. Be warned the sea can be quite rough but even on calm days there can be an strong undertow and there is a shelf with a step drop that goes from knee deep to overhead quite quickly.Lifeguards we're on duty. That said, it's one of those picture postcard sites you must visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Peace Haven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view from the mountain road is amazing and a fabulous photo opportunity. Lovely white part sandy/pebbly beach with turquoise water. Very quiet but we did visit on a Friday in June. Will probably be busier at weekends and height of season. There is nowhere to eat/drink so take your own provisions but there are toilets and parking available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful from afar, not so nice up close!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Like other reviews on here, the view of this beach from the mountain road is undoubtedly stunning. However, when we went down there later in the day, I was pretty disappointed! Yes the sea is wonderfully blue, but I have to say rather murky (definitely not for snorkelling) with some litter floating in it! And there are zero facilities except some rather overused toilets. To me, it also felt like a gravelly quarry when we were down there. I would say definitely worth a drive over to view it from the top, but if you do decide to venture down, make sure you have plenty of food, drinks (it’s especially hot due to the heat reflecting off the stone), a parasol (there are no naturally shaded areas), towels, flip flops (the stones are painful!), and a strong bladder.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If there was a paradise it sure would be Myrto beach in kephalonia! Breathtaking view with tuirquose water ,like being at the edge of the earth! Simply amazing'

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well deserved ‘must see’ beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No visit to Kefalonia would be complete without checking out Myrtos Beach. Brilliant white, rounded pebbles make for the most amazing azure sea. Steep descent so perhaps not for nervous drivers but safe enough if you take your time and don’t be distracted by the view!  Basic and disgusting toilet facility at back of beach but this is intended to be an unspoilt, uncommercialised, Captain Correlli beach. Changing facility in middle of beach - if this includes decent toilets I stand corrected!Lasting memories if you swim here believe me.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful for sure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is gorgeous no doubt. On the road to the beach there's a view point that has stunning views of the beach below. The down side is that the sea is very choppy /rough, and it seems its like this all around the year. No showers, no sun beds and on top of that it's a pebble beach so it's not the most comfortable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty but no facilities.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful from the road above, a bit of a let down when you get down there unless you like lying in a gravel pit. Hate to think what the loos were like.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a photo stop on the Tui premium island tour. Boy its breathtakinging beautiful... Captain Corellis beach. The sea is so many shades of torquoise. It would be accesible by car down a steepish winding road. No beds umbrellas or cafes, very few people. Just a stunning get away from it all place. From our photo stop point the smell of the sea and wild thyme completed the picture for me

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Romance with Captain Corelli
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We hired a car and drove to Mythos Beach. Not disappointed. The water was warm and inviting. The drive down to the beach not for the faint hearted. Definitely worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach used in captain Corelli mandolin film. Crystal clear seas and lovely blue tones, looks like the Caribbean, Lovely spot to visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excelent beach, do not expect that you can use the toilets. I don’t why they don’t put a tax for toiletes in order to be clean..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OMG Stunning... white beach and crystel clear blue waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: after popping into Assos we came here... oh my... I really cant put into words how utterly beautiful this beach is... no beds or bars etc, so take a cool bag drinks and get an umbrella from the local shop... this way you can stay longer and enjoy the stunning beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach. We love it. Waters crystal clear. Pity there are no facilities. Would be great to have a small taverna for water and snacks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: breathtaking but can be dangerous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most photographed beach of Kefalonia! And it is stunning with the turquoise water, steep cliffs and white beach. If you are driving around the island, make sure you stop above the beach to take photos. For swimming its not the best beach though, it can get rather dangerous with high waves and strong currents. What from above looks like sand is actually white pebbles which makes it hard to get out of the water. Good to know: Winding roads down to the beach Be careful! Myrtos is very affected by weather and wind - don't swim if the flag is red! Definitely not ideal for small kids.Facilities are limited (depends of the season). In the high season the beach struggles with wasps. Can be difficult to find a parking.The perfect time to go to Myrtos would be a windless day in the end of the season when the water is warm and the most people and cars are gone (and hopefully the wasps).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mighty myrtos not for the bare footed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome location,sandwiched between two mountains ,from above it looks crystal clear with fine white sand ,but in reality it's a stone filled beach ,with stones all the way too the breakwater ,kids wouldn't be safe swimming as the waves are huge ,some as big as four feet and crash onto the beach at very quick intervals ,I am a strong swimmer but found myself unable to get out to calmer water ,although a few hardy people did ,all in all I'd say visit some of the easier beaches particularly near Sami as they were all sand and easy to swim in ,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, great swim! But take food and drink as there's no bar or restaurants. Especially if you're travelling by bus as the walk to the nearest village is a long one up the mountain, so you are pretty much stuck there until your bus collects you. Also, take beach shoes as the pebbles going into the sea hurt your feet!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach, amazing clear water and very few tourists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great day on myrtos beach. Was able to drive down to and park really close to the beach. Bring your own umbrella though as there is very little shade available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You MUST GO
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You must go there for sure! Just choose a day with out a wind otherwise is dangerous! The waves will not let you go out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Supposedly the best in the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very big beach but very stony so not good for us. Petani is better. There is parking nearby. Not much in the way if refreshments by the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awestruck
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Truley a wonder of the natural world. One of the most beautiful beaches in the world . Crystal turquoise waters white sand amazing x

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped here for a quick swim as we passed. What an amazing place. Wonderful clear warm sea.Quite pebbly underfoot, but the views and sea make up for that

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sadly nothing really exists there anymore for such a stunning location. You would think the locals would of capitalised after the filming of “Captain Corelli’s Mandolin” In the short period we were there loads of tourists came down but soon left

reviewsWithKeywords.title: World class
reviewsWithKeywords.text: View from the top is amazing 😉 , and the drive down is spectacular, beautiful beach 🏖 we got there early so it was quiet 🤫 you would enjoy it better if you take water shoes it’s a pebble beach albeit small pebbles , take a parasol there is no natural shade . Worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Driving in a hire car, we eventually found the turn off to Myrtos Beach but our mistakes gave us beautiful views over it first. The steep road down was a bit hair raising, but we made it!!  No shade on the beach so only stayed 2 hours but worth the trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach probably best viewed from afar. There is a very good viewing area on the main road to the north of the beach. Waters are turquoise set off beautifully by white shore and not spoilt by rows of sun beds (at least in May). If you do decide to venture down tempted by the turquoise water as we were, you will be faced with a fairly narrow road with hairpins (well this is Kefalonia!). Once there there was a small area for parking. Beach actually consists of small pebbles and is quite uncomfortable to walk on. However, for somewhere so attractive, it was not crowded. Sea was calm and nice temperature to swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: To start the drive down was nerve racking, except for me driving, the cliff roads towards the beach were on the edge and then down towards the beach were steep.However it was worth it for an amazing beachThe sea was lovely and not too wavy.It was crystal clear turquoise and a great swim.The beach was white and simple. No beach bars here. Worth a visit.Some fantastic photos, from the top and from the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here for a photo opportunity whilst on a tour of the island. The views are absolutely stunning really Beautiful, it's a must visit of you're in kefalonia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking Views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Myrtos beach during a family holiday in May you will need a car to get to the beach, the drive down to the beach itself is pretty spectacular and you have to stop to take photos.  The beach itself is small stones so would take beach shoes to avoid painful feet.  I don't think the beach would be suitable for young children as the waves were dumping on the beach quite strongly during our visit and there were no sunbed or facilities but this could have been due to the fact it was early in the season.Well worth a visit for the views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I went on an island tour and this beach is a must.  If you visit Kefalonia put this on your list.  The beach is stunning and the different shades of blue in the sea is amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see beach apparently!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove from the North up to Myrtos and Assos. A fantastic drive. Lots of hair-pin bends so drive carefully. And watch out for rocks on the road.Pull over safely at the top before descending and see the best views of the beach. Blue Sea against a white pebble beach looks amazing.Drive down for limited parking. There is no shade apart from the cave at the end. But be careful as rocks fall down all the time near the cave, great views inside and water in there too.Cool clear water and nice for swimming. A Stony beach so not comfortable. But OK. We went in the morning at 11am.. Not busy in May! So parked easily. Not sure where cars park in Peak season once full!We headed to Assos after here, which is amazing. More scary driving, but take it slowly and you'll be fine.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the view of the beach is breathe taking and well worth the visit to swim in the crystal clear waters is lovely there are no toilets or shop there

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and clearblue water!You can see the beach from a hill and then you can go down to the beach.Good road so it’s No problems with drivning down.It’s a must see place on Kefalonia!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow wow and wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The trip down to the beach is hazardous but well worth it but a word of warning not good for children or adults that can't swim very deep water straight away as one walks in

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everything you've read, heard seen on the television does not do justice to this breathtaking view. Its certainly worth a visit and make sure you take your camera.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful from a height.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped here to look over this amazing looking beach but did not bother with going down as it is a pebble beach and it can get very busy. The water is a stunning colour and looks inviting but is a little tricky to get down to as there is only one road you can use t get on to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: OMG, the sea here beats even the Maldives!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach, well worth the near motion sickness getting to it!!My only complaint.. there are not that many fishes in the sea!! Honestly though, can’t fault itPs beware: no shade or shelter, or places to buy water on the beach so bring your own!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazingly beautiful beach where the white gravel - wouldn't call it sand, creates the most azure blue sea. This is the problem! It gets so busy on the beach that it is not relaxing at all. We lasted ½ hour then left for a quieter beach. A must see mind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We didn't go onto the actual beach as the coach could not get down there but we stopped for a photostop and it is beautiful!It is defiantly worth a stop there to just see it for yourself!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must-see when in Kephalonia! The turquoise and blue water against the white stones is so beautiful, even on a cloudy day. There is a place to park and take some photos up top off the main road. The drive down was much easier than I expected from the other reviews. Don't try to go barefoot or you will have very sore feet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous For It’s Beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtle beach is always featured in travel brochures and this is because it is so beautiful when viewed from above. One day we decided to go to the beach to see it properly. The sand was clean  and it was a lovely beach for families because the sea was not deep at the edge of the beach. The road down to the beach was steep and the cars were parking at the bottom of the hill actually on the beach. It would be nicer to have a carpark specifically for the beach without intruding on to the sand in cars

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOW!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This just took our breath away! Approaching it from the main road we pulled over and looked down onto the beach below and just knew we had to go down to walk on the beautiful white sand. The sea was a bright turquoise colour and just as in the pictures we had seen advertising Kefalonia. The road down is very winding with some very acute bends but worth every minute. We walked along the sands and everyone we spoke to was just as in awe of the scenery as we were...in particular a guy from Panama!Highly recommend a trip here ...you will not be disappointed!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a fantastic drive along the coast road to get here with breathtaking views. The road down from the village to the beach is steep but take care and it's fine. You will realise when you go down why coaches can't get there but this makes the place more special as there isn't coach loads of people. The beach is mainly pebbles and shingle and the sea gets deep quite quickly.Well worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOW Stunning Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked from Agia Efimia (crazy idea but we managed!) the views from the top are amazing, the colour of the sea is unbelievable. We walked down to the beach and had not brought swim shoes! As we were travelling light! Big mistake! The pebbles absolutely kill your feet and they shift when you walk on them so it’s hard to get out. Be careful the waves are so strong and the undertow could feel a little scary Well worth visiting the locals pride and joy! They often ask if you’ve been.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited Myrtos beach and the drive down to the parking was breath taking. Views of the beach are amazing especially how the colours are so indistinctive, was truly worth the visit.If staying in Skala it is about one hour drive and is totally recommended for visit. The beach was clean and nice, able to swim.The only let down to the beach is the fact that the toilet and changing facility have not been maintained - hence why the 3* and not 5*. The beach itself is definitely worth the 5* but the experience that me and a friend had visiting the WC facility was horrific. The toilets were all closed(locked) so unable to gain any access to them. The only one that was open was awful and sickening to see. The changing area also smelt and seemed like it was used as an excretion area instead of the closed toilets.Would recommend going to a WC before attending the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just amazing. Would suggest to have swim shoes to spare your feet especially if you are not use to walking barefoot, with you as the beach is sandy and full of pebbles. Most beautiful white pebbles. Also be careful it  starts shallow and then sudden deap drop into the ocean. But worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I'm sure it's all been said before
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best beach I have ever seen the view from above is amazing if your in a car do drive down the dodgy windy road to have a walk along it the sea is the craziest colour I've ever seen truly beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just back from the fabulous island of kefelonia and will return , myrtos beach is an absolute must one of the best of many beautiful beeches on the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large, famous beach that has beautiful pebbles, unfortunately no sand so beach/sea shoes strongly recommended. Very pretty small cave area at southern end of the beach for special photos. Virtually empty on a sunny warm day early April. Wierd seeing mountain goats coming down onto the beach area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradiso
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Un po’ difficile da raggiungere, ma quando ci arrivi sembra un posto fuori dal nulla, acque limpidissime ed onde mozzafiato, ci ritorneremo sicuramente.A bit 'difficult to reach, but when you get there seems a place out of nowhere, crystal clear waters and breathtaking waves, we will definitely return

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the drive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to this beach just to take photos and it did not disappoint. It is beautiful and the drive down is lovely. Well worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but be aware of rip tides
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was there a few years back and the sea although not rough the waves were quite big due to the steep angle of the beach going in to the sea, I got caught out by a rip tide and luckily didn't panic 'too much' and waited until the sea "let me go" about 100 metres out, didn't bother going back in, not something ill forget in a hurry. Stunning place to visit, yes the approach road is a bit dicey, but take your time and it will be fine. Stay in your depth if the waves are misbehaving!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach...Wild and Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Beach is a prized beach and one of the earthly paradises!!!In one contest it came first in Europe and in another 3rd worldwide.The scenery is incredible whether you take photos from the top or drive down to the beach.However if you decide to drive down have in mind that you'll have to extra careful of the road-it's not in the best condition.You'll also find that a lot of fences have been put up in places to keep rocks from falling-which happens every time there's an earthquake.No surprise there.But the beach itself compensates you!White sand and pebbles all along the beach and crystal clear waters.Restrict yourselves to the middle of the beach and avoid the sides at the far end due to small avalanches.It would be wise not going very deep.The waters may be shallow at first but they suddenly get  a bit steep especially if it's a windy day .If you have small children,just keep them restricted to the shallow part.In any case,it's an experience not to be missed.Photos of Myrtos do not do it justice-it's far more beautiful in real life!!!It's also one of the areas where the filming took place of Captain Koreli's Mandolin starring Nicholas Cage and Penelope Cruise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos beach is without doubt the most beautiful beach in Greece and one of the most dramatic. Before heading to Myrtos beach try to drive to the panorama viewpoint seen on the way to Assos, i.e. after passing Divarata. The breathtaking view daytime is stunning. The sunset from the same viewpoint attracts people from all around the Island. The beach is crowded daytime,  but very peaceful after 18 p.m for those who want to enjoy the ambience in harmony with nature and the surrounding mountains. The Myrtos Bay is backed by steep limestone cliffs. Dedicate at least one day for Myrtos Beach and its surroundings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Beach is absolutely beautiful! The bluest and cleanest water! Best to pack a picnic lunch and plenty of water as there isn't much around at all. Another idea would be to bring a beach tent/umbrella. I didn't spend much time at this beach so I didn't need any of the above..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was beautiful - but it is stone and not sand so it made itDifficult to walk on. It was very busy and the sea was clear and blue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unbelievably beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a beautiful beach! But come prepared with sun shades, chairs/sunbeds, towels, water, food etc because there is nothing else there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos Beach is beautiful and worth a visit but don't expect to stay very long. The views are stunning but when we visited at the end of May there was no sunbeds or umbrellas making it impossible to sunbath unless you took your own. There is no taverner or shop on the beach so make sure you stock up on supplies before driving down the long, steep winding road!There is a beautiful view point from the road at the top looking down onto the beach if you don't fancy the drive down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better from above...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's the backdrop that makes this a stunning view. It's a long way down, and in my opinion, not worth the trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A gorgeous beach with white gravel like marble, the water is very deep at the shore, but since it is ff salty it's not a problem! The problem is that you do not find a parking space, you have to bring your sun umbrella becouse sun is hot and so do not miss the drinks because there are no shops or restaurants!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach worth the steep winding decent. Not the biggest beach I. Imagine it's busy in the summer.  I went in April before the tourist season so it was almost deserted, but still just about warm enough to swim. I highly recommend paragliding for more amazing views!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view from above as you drive down to tis beach is stunning.  It is a small narrow twisty road with many switchbacks, not easy to do up or down but undoubtedly worth the effort.  There are many facilities on the beach so if you can bring food and drink with you.The sea is a stunning blue, it is not a sandy beach but tiny white gritty stuff.make the effort for the day and get out to this stunning beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and setting, could be better cleanliness and water clarity
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely setting and easy to get to.Beach itself is mixture of sand and pebbles.The shop/cafe was shut when we went and facilities close except for 1 which had been broken open plus had no water so was not at all pleasant.There was some litter left in the beach and the water was murky with white dust so was good to swim but not snorkel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great scenery but not for swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited on a windy day in October. The scenery was spectacular and the pebbly beach attractive but the waves and pebbly beach made it dangerous and painful to get in and out of the sea. Only four lads went in while we were there and one had difficulty getting out. At the end of October all facilities except one WC were closed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We recently visited this beach and unfortunately we were disappointed . There is no doubt that the view from above is stunning and the colour of the sea is turquoise blue . However as you descend to the beach it loses its charm . It's still a nice beach but by no means fabulous . We found another beach near Sami which was beautiful  and that we much preferred ( antisamos beach)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing deep blue sea like in a dream
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First you need to catch the view from the top. It's just amazing and incredible how blue and pure it is.. Then go down on the beach. Can be wavy, but so nice !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but paddling is painful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach, turquoise waters leading to deep blue water. Beach is very pebbley which is painful underfoot. Taverna and toilets in summer, nothing in Winter.  Easy to park in winter. Lots of photo opportunities on main road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Colours
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had heard about this beach as being one of the top 10 in the world, so we HAD to see it for ourselves. We drove the coast road up from Agostoli. To say it was an experience is an understatement. We are both not the best with heights and not realising that this coast road was so high, it was quite an unnerving drive. Rock falls, missing barriers, coach drivers coming towards you with one hand on the wheel and the other holding a mobile phone!!!! It was a relief to get there. It's a steep road down with plenty of hairpin bends and there is a small car park at the bottom. Ok in October but in July/August must be a nightmare. The colour of the water is fantastic. I've never seen sea like it. Every hue of blue imaginable - absolutely gorgeous. Be warned though it is a pebbly beach and the surf is strong enough to knock you off your feet.(Some kind of footwear is advisable). Once past the break though it's relatively calm. There are shops just off the coast rode just before you get to the beach, that sell beach equipment and toys. Overall though the beach is definitely worth a visit if just for the stunning views, but one of the worlds top 10 hmmm not so sure. PS we found out afterward that there is a cross country road that we could have used. DOH!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stay up and take a photo.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a very pebbly beach with strong waves - pretty from above but for a visit you're better off driving elsewhere!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Second best beach in Greece!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are two greatest beaches in Greece: Egremnoi and Myrtos. I was very lucky to swim on the first one before the earthquake of 2015/11/17 destroyed it forever and I had a chance to have a glimpse of Myrtos from the viewpoint during my one day’s trip to Kefalonia  from Zakynthos. As compared to Egremnoi, Myrtos seems to be a shorter, but wider. And it has pebbles in a jumble with sand whereas Egremnoi had small white pebbles only – so soft and pleasant for your feet...The water in both places is just stunning: Nice is nervously smoking on the sidelines - for sure! :) :) :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: holiday october 2017
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach, amazing views from the top of the cliffs. very clean, crystal clear water, the road in is  very steep and twisting......nit for the faint hearted

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just look at it!Went for a short visit a couple of days ago, nice and quiet this time of year but still beautiful - didn’t have any problems parking right on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Much more scenic from the cliff
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No doubt about it this beach is a photographer idea of heaven!  Although it looks tricky to get to it wasn't that bad - a steep winding road but wide enough for two cars to pass comfortably!  We had no problem parking but I imagine it gets very busy in the main holiday season.  The beach is actually rather rocky and pebbly when you get onto it - but it does look lovely.  It has tavernas and facilities with beds and parasols.  The waves were very rough and as I'm not a strong swimmer I only paddled.  I noticed that getting in was much easier than getting out - many people struggled with the powerful waves knocking them over onto the rough pebbles.  I was pleased that I visited but I think I would just stop at the top to look next time!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtakingly beautiful Myrthos Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrthos Beach is absolutely beautiful. The colours of the sea are simply stunning! The beach has small pebbles so do protect your feet!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning location.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach with wow factor location. Azure blue sea and golden beach. Stony with sand. Steep gradient once in water so quickly out if your depth. Appears sheltered from the tide on day of visit. Sunbeds and umbrellas available for a fee. Showers and toilets/changing cubicles FOC on beach. Small kiosk for food and drink about 5 min uphill walk from beach. A definite must if anywhere near.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but not the best for swimming.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach after a very steep descent which I wouldn't like to do in high season! Amazing panoramic views from up top. Beautiful clear water and lovely white pebbles. No taverna, but toilets and changing rooms are there. Sunbeds if you want them. Not much parking so not sure how it would be in august. Steep shelf into  the water with Quite strong currents and a strong undertow , not for a weak swimmer or someone unsteady on their feet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Myrtos beach is breathtaking! Both from looking at the turquoise see from above and being on the beach itself! You need swimming shoes as the see it pebbly and be aware to dips quickly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turquoise heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For a very long time Myrtos seemed almost mythical to me. Here I was in rainy London and there was this place, miles away, with this impossibly turquoise blue sea and stunning backdrop. I was longing to get there and when I finally did, I thought I was in heaven. You see, I'm a proper beach bum (are you allowed to say 'bum' on TripAdvisor? ) and I do love when sea is perfectly blue. It is a beautiful, stunning, gorgeous, incredible place and no wonder it is often mentioned in the best beaches category. I was lucky to visit Myrtos beach twice during my past holiday. From what I hear, I was also lucky to be able to swim there (day one only). The waves were way too big the next day. Having said that, the beach still looked beautiful and I did some paragliding with 'No Borders' team who were there that day (big shout out to them, they were fantastic!).From the more practical point of view, the beach was easy to find, the road leading to it not scary at all and there was no problem with parking space (mid August). No umbrellas/sun loungers so bring your own. There are 2 viewpoints up the hill, one of each side and they are a must stop for the one last photo of this stunning beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: superb visa
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The visa from the top of the hill overlooking the bay is wonderful. The clear water shows a sandy shelving beach clear of rocks except for the edges. The road down to the beach may be a no-no for nervous drivers. When down on the beach one may be disappointed how commercialised it is with taverna and beach umbrellas but I guess that's what one has to expect.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches i have seen.On windy days it is quite dangerous as the waves could reach the hight if 2-3m.A must see place . You need to know swimming to use the water as it deeps down dramatically a couple of meter away from beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking Location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most fantastic location with white pebbles and turquoise sea, fantastic views over the headlands.  There is parking at the beach.  Need shoes to get to the sea as very pebbly.  The sea dips quickly so there is surf to get through when swimming.  there is a small beach cafe, limited toilets and changing facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking view from above and below
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sun shining on the beach and sea when we pulled up off the road at a viewing place above the beach, made us take a breath, it's a wow factor!   The road to the area and down to the beach is pretty scary at times and not for the faint hearted.  We were lucky that it was quiet when we visited and fairly easy to drive there without meeting anyone coming the other way!  It's definitely worth the drive though and once down on the beach we were surprised how big the waves are and how dramatic it is.  The sea is not good for swimming unless you are a strong swimmer as the waves are big and strong and there's a ledge which drops down when entering the sea.  The beach is pebbly/stony which explains the white nature of it.  There are facilities on site such as toilets and a café bar.  I saw a bus come down to the beach too so presumably there is a bus service though not sure how often this runs.  The car parking was ok for us as it wasn't too busy but not sure what it will be like at the height of summer and popular times.  The parking is free of charge.  There is no shelter from the sun either so be prepared.  It was one of the nicest beaches however on the island and should not be missed - even if you just view from above.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Myrtos Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must visit Beach on this gorgeous island of Kafelonia ! Clear blue sea , with white sand. Plenty of sun beds and umbrellas to hire ! Safe for swimming with a majestic landscape as a back drop. Lots of great restaurants nearby for fantastic Greek food to enjoy when you leave the beach !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful places to see on the island! Crystal clear water and breath taking views on the way to the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos Beach / Pylaros
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beach like a super postcard or for never-ending holidays; rocks and high cliffs, deep blue sea; there are sunbeds to rent; is a sandy with pebble beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Travelling up to fiscardo we decided to pull over and take pictures from above of Myrtos beach which looked absolutely amazing, but little did we know that we could drive down to the beach AND there was free parking too.Beach was gorgeous and wasnt packed at all, and the sea was piercing blue.Spent a couple of hours here, pure bliss.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Posers Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's only wonderful from the high cliff tops. Once down on the beach it is full of posing "beach professionals". It's mostly pebbly and what sand there is, is sharp and uncomfortable to walk on. There are plenty of better options that are quieter and with fewer "pouches" on display.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The more times You come the more MAGICAL it gets!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a chameleon beach! No wonder it is one of the most beautiful beaches on planet earth!At first I wasn't impressed much...yes, the color of the sea is turquoise/marine blue combination - beautiful when seen from one of the 2 spots on the main road above the beach...but than you reach the beach and think to yourself "oh, well, these pebbles hurt my legs" and although there is sand in the middle of the beach You still have to walk the pebbles to reach the water. Some good water snickers made this no longer a problem! We bought ours for 10euros pair and that was great because we used them on other beaches too! (most beaches in Kefalonia have pebbles, especially those on the north and west side)And than, because we were situated in the village just above Myrthos, we were passing by every day, we started seeing the colors change, in the morning and during sunset, when it was windy and wavy and when the sea was calm and actually it looked its best when there were high waves and it was sunny, the colors looked like if a painter was drawing his painting! Absolutely magical!The beach is highly acoustical so the sound of the waves is miraculous!For the bathing part, it is a bit tricky if You are not a good swimmer and it is not that suitable for little kids as the water gets deep fast. The water was good temperature in September, not cold while the sea was calm and pretty warm when there were waves.There are sun beds in the middle of the beach, but we didn't use them, with a small restaurant/cafe, we didn't try it either. There is no natural shade on the beach from 11-14 so either bring a parasol or hide in the little cave on the left side of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEAUTIFUL!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is just spectacular!  The water is an incredible blue, to rival any I have seen in Mauritius and the Maldives.  Take your beach shoes though as there are some pebbles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What amazing views. Definitely take water shoes as suggested in other reviews very pebbly beach. Take lunch and drinks and just enjoy the day there swimming in turquoise waters. Well worth a day out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my top 5!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived in Kefalonia to high waves and choppy waters for 4 days down in the south of the island. We spent those days searching out little coves with calm waters. Finally, the weather changed and it was time to visit Myrtos Beach, a "must see" on my list when planning this trip. As you drive down the twisting roads with hairpin turns, you catch a glimpse of the brilliant blue waters, white shore and high cliffs. Stunning. Breathtaking!In September there were plenty of places to park, no problem. The beach consists of pure white pebbles which is hard to walk on barefoot, but most people use water shoes or leave their flip flops near the water when they swim. The water is CRYSTAL clear and warm. We loved this beach so much we came back the next day!I've been to many beaches in my life, in all different parts of the world,  and Myrtos Beach is definitely up there in my all time top 5 favorites. Wish I was there now!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best view on beach, take parashute
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice view on the beach from top, small white stones not sandy, beautiful most torquize blue water you ever saw, must do is a parashute from top of the hill to the beach. Take camera and just enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Having viewed the beach from above we decided to venture down the narrow road to the beach itself, looks a worse drive than it is and well worth it, get there early as parking becomes crowded and enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were very disappointed with this beach. Looking down at it from the road but once down there it's really not a very nice beach. It is a mainly pebble beach, but it resembles a builders yard. There are toilets. No food or drink facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As we drove down the mountain to the beach, the view takes your breath away! It is definitely worth going to. Take water and snacks with you as there is no restaurants on the beach but that adds to the charm . Beach shoes help walk on the pebbles! You can even go paragliding of the cliff, which of course I had to try and loved it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Looks spectacular from above
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Looks spectacular from above at road level with white sand and crystal clear blue and turquoise water. Beach is white but very stoney so you need suitable footwear to walk on it.at the time we visited the refreshment area was being refurbished so had to leave early but lovely location.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went as part of a tour of the island with Avgerinos travel experience based in SamiWell worth going on as we got to see this wonderful beach would definitely recommend seeing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Call that a beach?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best beach on the island, so they say. It is a pretty little crescent shaped beach, with a few rows of sunbeds and straw umbrellas. It also has great views but on the grand scale of magnificent beaches, it falls well short.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely Stunning Beach with a spectacular sunset!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A visit to Myrtos beach is a must while you are in Kefalonia island! There is plenty of car park space free of charge. The beach is stunning with tirquase crystal clear waters!! The only drawback is that there is no restaurant, no sunbeds or umbrellas but as we told from locals they plan to make Myrtos beach an organised beach.  We were lucky that we saw an incredable sunset.  We visited the cave that was situated at the very end of beach which was pretty amazing!! Love this beach!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An incredible place!  Unlike Petani bay, there are no restaurants, chairs/umbrellas.  You still need you water shoes, this is not a sandy beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very disappointing visit this year...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately, this year, there is NO BEACH BAR at all, so when you go to Myrtos, take your own drinks and snacks. Additionally, there is a minimal amount of sunbeds and umbrellas available for rent this year, maybe half of what there normally is. We got to the beach at 11.30am and there were no beds or umbrellas available, so we had a swim, sweltered in the sun for an hour and left. And, if you have sensitive feet, you MUST wear beach shoes, as the pebbles are really tough on your feet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this beach 12 years ago  it was stunning, very few people and sun beds. I was so disappointed this time roun. It is now completely in a state of disrepair. What looked like a bar is been dismantled, just half of it, there are still WC facilities, but looks very dirty overall. The view from  above is still breathtaking so at least you have a wonderful photo.I do hope that can the restored to its former and natural beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely to look at but beware
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely to look at but a nightmare to walk on, make sure you take the Jelly Shoes that you can wear on the stony beach and into the water. Nearly crippled me walking down to the sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Describing Myrtos beach as "paradise on earth" these are the right words for this lovely and wonderful beach in KefaloniaThe water is clear, diferent blue color tonality, super clean with wonderful sunset.Not to be missed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning, the sea is an unbelievable colour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is a must to visit, the scenery and views are outstanding, the only downside is the stones are sharp under foot making access to the sea ouchie with out decent foot wear. The sea was warm but can be rough with a strong current.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach we've visited
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After a stunning drive down to the beach itself,we found quite a lot of cars parked but the beach size still makes it feel quiet! The colours of the sea will stay with the wife and I for a long time! A must visit for all who come to kefalonia!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Myrtos beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful place.Dont be fooled by the white beach It is pebbles and boulders. But even that said it is a fabulous place to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but slightly scary drive down the hairpin bends. As with everywhere on Kephalonia the parking is free. Also great views of it from the main road at the top if you didn't fancy the drive down.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Iconic beach but be careful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: from the hillside the beach looks fantastic and the colour of the water is amazing. the beach is shingle so can be hard on your feet if not wearing water shoes. When we visited the water was quite rough and was breaking on the shore with 4 foot waves which made getting into and out of the water tricky. we didn't see any warning flags or life guards, there is no cafe or bar although there was some toilets that you could use if you could hold your breathe long enough as they did smell quite badly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the most photographed beach in Greece, and described as one of the most dramatic, Myrtos's mile-and-a-half long arc of dazzling white pebbles is an assault on the senses.Whilst it's stunningly beautiful the combination of pebbles, shelving and strong currents mean you have to take real care - especially with the children.It's very exposed – although umbrellas are available for hire.A beach bar and toilet provides everything a sun-worshipper should need.During September it was fairly busy, I can imagine that in high season it's rammed.If you want to take the easy photographic option park up in the lay-by on the main road and shoot away.It really is a visually stunning beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach - Cristal clear water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful beach with Cristal clear water. Nicest beach in Kefalonia.Free parking space.Little wite stones on the beach No bar or restaurant at the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most breathtaking beach in Europe
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach, big peoples and steep slopes but the drive down to it off the mountain will take your breath away x

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visually stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented a scooter to travel around Cephalonia.  The steep road down to the beach suddenly reveals on precipitous lay-bys  the turquoise & azure waves breaking on the beach far below. The sheer size & area of the turquoise surf is startling. There was a strong onshore wind which meant the waves were vertically dumping their full force on the pebbles & there was a undertow, so no one was in the water. This was disappointing, but nothing could detract from the amazingly beautiful turquoise colour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach view overlook ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a chilly day in October when we visited, so we didn't want to spend any time on a beach, but the view from above was amazing.  There's an overlook where you can stop to get a photo that includes all the vivid blues you can imagine in the water, along with mountains, clouds, outlying islands - it's just a gorgeous view.  If you watch the movie Captain Corelli's Mandolin with Nicholas Cage and Penelope Cruz (and pretty much the only reason to watch it is if you're planning a visit) you'll have fallen in love with this view long before you get there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view, but that's about it..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views of this iconic beach are amazing! You will need a car to get down to it or a pair of pretty good trainers/hiking boots! And watch out for the goats along the way!This beach has supreme views and is a must for a photo happy tourist! From above, what looks like sand is actually fairly white pebbles.
